     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
     4	# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
     5	#
     6	# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
     7	# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
     8	# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
     9	# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
    10	# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
    11	# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
    12	# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
    13	# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
    14	#
    15	# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
    16	# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
    17	#
    18	# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
    19	# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
    20	# =============================================================================
    21	set -euo pipefail
    22	export LC_ALL=C
    23	
    24	ROOT="."
    25	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    26	  case "$1" in
    27	    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    28	    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    29	    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    30	  esac
    31	done
    32	PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
    33	[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
    34	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }
    35	
    36	keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
    37	[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }
    38	# Alternation of the dot-escaped keys; each must be preceded by a dot that is
    39	# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
    40	alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)
    41	pattern="(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)"
    42	
    43	hits=$(cd "$ROOT" && grep -rnE "$pattern" .claude tools 2>/dev/null \
    44	  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?\.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib\.sh:' \
    45	  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?tools/check-knob-readers\.sh:' || true)
    46	if [[ -n "$hits" ]]; then
    47	  echo "check-knob-readers.sh: direct read(s) of a profile key; use loa_knob from .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:" >&2
    48	  printf '%s\n' "$hits" | cut -c1-240 >&2
    49	  exit 1
    50	fi
    51	echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no direct profile-key reads ($(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') keys checked)"

+#   interpreter — body scanned exactly as today: the header holds `$(`, a

+#     continues on the next line (`|`, `&&`, `||` last) or an earlier line
+#     opened a substitution, group, quote or pipe; a member of the heredoc's
+#     pipeline is a shell, interpreter, wrapper that runs its argument or SQL
+#     runner (_bdb_hd_is_interp, _bdb_hd_is_runner); an allowlisted form
+#     carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag (-c, -e, -x clusters, --exec,
+#     --eval, --command, in-place); a write target is executable content

+#     shebang; the body holds `<<` (nested); a target's basename appears
+#     elsewhere in the command outside the safe readers (_bdb_hd_same_line_exec:

+#     (_bdb_hd_member): cat, tee, printf, echo with plain-file or stdout sinks;
+#     gh pr|issue comment -F -; gh pr create --body-file -; git commit -F -;
+#     br create|update reading `-`; jq/yq without in-place; grep; sed -n with
+#     a print-only script; sort; wc. The body is then scanned PER SEGMENT
+#     (_bdb_hd_scan_body): each line split on ; && || | &, wrapper prefixes
+#     stripped (sudo command exec env nice time nohup builtin stdbuf ionice,
+#     a leading backslash, quote, paren or brace, assignments, an absolute
+#     path); a segment whose command word is a fence verb (rm git find dd
+#     mkfs* shred truncate kubectl terraform aws gcloud psql mysql DROP
+#     DELETE TRUNCATE) is kept on its own line for the normal rules, other
+#     segments are dropped. The body falls back to a full scan when it holds
+#     `$(`, a backtick, `<(` or `>(` under an unquoted delimiter, or a segment
+#     word is an interpreter or wrapper, or a variable (`$x -rf /`; such a
+#     segment is ALSO scanned as rm, git and kubectl with the same arguments).
+#     Special case (the #1245 scrub): a standalone quoted-delimiter `cat`
+#     whose header is exactly `cat <<'W' [> path]` drops the whole body.
+#   none — the consumer is on neither list: full scan.
+# Documented gap: a body written to a plain file by one command and executed
+# by a LATER command is outside a per-command fence (the Write tool shares it).
+# =============================================================================
+_bdb_hd_op_re='^[0-9]*(<<<|<<-|&>>|<<|>>|>[|]|&&|[|][|]|[|]&|&>|<>|>&[0-9-]*|<&[0-9-]*|;;|;|&|[|]|<|>|[(]|[)])$'
+_bdb_hd_re_dw='^[A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+$'
+_bdb_hd_re_dsq="^'([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)'\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_ddq='^"([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)"$'
+_bdb_hd_re_dbs='^\\([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)$'
+_bdb_hd_re_psq="^'([^']*)'\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_pdq="^\"([^\"\$\`\\\\]*)\"\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_pbare="^[^'\"\$\`\\\\]+\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_ctl=$'[\x01-\x08\x0b-\x1f\x7f]'
+_bdb_hd_re_exflag='^-[A-Za-z]*[cex][A-Za-z]*$'
+_bdb_hd_re_exlong='^--(exec|eval|command|in-?place)'
+_bdb_hd_re_ext='\.(sh|bash|zsh|ksh|csh|fish|py|pyw|rb|pl|pm|js|mjs|cjs|ts|mts|cts|ps1|psm1|php|lua|tcl|command|bat|cmd)$'
+_bdb_hd_re_sys='(^|/)(\.claude/hooks(/|$)|\.claude/settings[^/]*\.json$|\.git/hooks(/|$)|\.git/config$|\.gitconfig$|\.ssh/rc$|\.config/(fish|zsh|bash|git)/|s?bin/[^/]+$)'
+_bdb_hd_re_rc='(^|/)\.(bashrc|bash_profile|bash_login|bash_logout|profile|zshrc|zshenv|zprofile|zlogin|zlogout|kshrc|mkshrc|cshrc|tcshrc|login|logout|envrc)$'
+_bdb_hd_re_sedp='^(([0-9]+|[$]|/[^/]*/)(,([0-9]+|[$]|/[^/]*/))?)?p$'
+_bdb_hd_re_assign='^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*='
+_bdb_hd_re_varw='^[$]([{]|[A-Za-z_])'
+_bdb_hd_re_knob='^[[:space:]]+heredoc_classifier:[[:space:]]*["'"'"']?([A-Za-z]+)["'"'"']?[[:space:]]*(#.*)?$'
+
+# Shells, interpreters and wrappers that run their argument or stdin.
+_bdb_hd_is_interp() {
+  case "$1" in
+    bash|sh|zsh|dash|ksh|mksh|ash|fish|csh|tcsh|busybox|python|python[0-9]*|pypy*|node|nodejs|deno|bun|ruby|irb|perl|php|lua|luajit|tclsh|wish|expect|pwsh|powershell|osascript|Rscript) return 0 ;;
+    eval|source|.|exec|command|builtin|time|awk|gawk|mawk|nawk|make|gmake|m4|ed|ex|vi|vim|nvim|gdb) return 0 ;;
+    sudo|doas|su|runuser|env|xargs|parallel|timeout|nohup|nice|ionice|setsid|stdbuf|chroot|unshare|nsenter|ssh|docker|podman|kubectl|find|watch|script) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+# The SQL runners of the FR-1.4/5/6 precondition (same list).
+_bdb_hd_is_runner() {
+  case "$1" in
+    psql|pgcli|mysql|mariadb|mysqlsh|sqlite3|sqlcmd|sqlplus|isql|usql|litecli|duckdb|clickhouse|clickhouse-client|cockroach|bq|wrangler|prisma|supabase|drizzle-kit|knex|sequelize|typeorm|flyway|liquibase|dbmate|goose|sqitch|rails|manage.py|artisan|alembic|dbt|atlas|mongosh|sqlx) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}

+_bdb_hd_is_destructive() {
+  case "$1" in
+    rm|git|find|dd|shred|truncate|kubectl|terraform|aws|gcloud|psql|mysql|mkfs|mkfs.*) return 0 ;;

+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+# Readers that may name a heredoc's target elsewhere on the line.
+_bdb_hd_is_safe_reader() {
+  case "$1" in
+    cat|ls|wc|head|tail|grep|egrep|fgrep|rg|diff|cmp|stat|file|test|'['|echo|printf|sort|uniq|jq|yq|git|gh|br|mkdir|touch|realpath|readlink|basename|dirname|du|md5sum|sha1sum|sha256sum|shasum|b2sum|cksum) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_tokenize <line> → _bdb_hd_tok[] (words keep their quotes; operators
+# are separate tokens, an fd number joins its redirect). Returns 1 when the
+# line cannot be read: open quote, trailing backslash, unquoted comment.
+_bdb_hd_tokenize() {
+  local s="${1:-}" n i=0 ch tok="" q="" have=0 op cand
+  n=${#s}
+  _bdb_hd_tok=()
+  while (( i < n )); do
+    ch="${s:i:1}"
+    if [[ -n "$q" ]]; then
+      tok="$tok$ch"
+      if [[ "$q" == "'" ]]; then
+        [[ "$ch" == "'" ]] && q=""
+      elif [[ "$ch" == '\' ]]; then
+        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
+        i=$((i + 1)); tok="$tok${s:i:1}"
+      elif [[ "$ch" == '"' ]]; then
+        q=""
+      fi
+      i=$((i + 1)); continue
+    fi
+    case "$ch" in
+      "'"|'"') q="$ch"; tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      '\')
+        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
+        tok="$tok$ch${s:i+1:1}"; have=1; i=$((i + 2)) ;;
+      ' '|$'\t')
+        if (( have )); then _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"; tok=""; have=0; fi
+        i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      '#')
+        (( have )) || return 1
+        tok="$tok$ch"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      ';'|'&'|'|'|'<'|'>'|'('|')')
+        op=""
+        for cand in '<<<' '<<-' '&>>' '<<' '>>' '>|' '&&' '||' '|&' '&>' '<>' '>&' '<&' ';;' ';' '&' '|' '<' '>' '(' ')'; do
+          if [[ "${s:i:${#cand}}" == "$cand" ]]; then op="$cand"; break; fi
+        done
+        i=$((i + ${#op}))

+          while (( i < n )) && [[ "${s:i:1}" == [0-9-] ]]; do op="$op${s:i:1}"; i=$((i + 1)); done
+        fi
+        if (( have )); then
+          if [[ "$tok" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$op" == '<'* || "$op" == '>'* ]]; then
+            op="$tok$op"
+          else
+            _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
+          fi
+          tok=""; have=0
+        fi
+        _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$op" ;;
+      *) tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+    esac
+  done

+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_unq_path <word> → _hd_up; returns 1 for a non-literal path (an
+# expansion, an escape, mixed quoting) or an empty one.
+_bdb_hd_unq_path() {

+# content (or cannot be judged).
+_bdb_hd_exec_dest() {

+    *'*'*|*'?'*|*'['*|*'{'*|'~'|'~'[!/]*|'') return 0 ;;

+  else d="${PWD:-.}"
+  fi

+  done

+# _bdb_hd_member <tokens…> → _hd_mcls (interpreter|nonexec|none) for one
+# pipeline member; write targets are appended to _hd_dests.

+    t="${argv[i]}"

+  done

+    cat)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do [[ "${argv[i]}" == "-" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; done ;;
+    tee)

+          -a|--append|-p) ;;
+          -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
+          *) _bdb_hd_unq_path "$t" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }

+        esac

+          -f|--file) [[ "${argv[1]}" == create && "${argv[i+1]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1 ;;

+# _bdb_hd_same_line_exec <basename> <header idx> <body first> <body last>

+# The #1245 header grammar (byte-identical to _bdb_scrub_cat_heredoc's).
+_bdb_hd_plain_cat() {
+  local header="${1:-}" marker candidate
+  local delimiter_re="<<(-?)('([[:alnum:]_]+)'|\"([[:alnum:]_]+)\")"
+  local path_re="([[:alnum:]_./-]+|'[[:alnum:]_ ./-]+'|\"[[:alnum:]_ ./-]+\")"

+# Only an explicit false|no|off turns it off; turning it off only tightens.
+_bdb_heredoc_knob_on() {
+  local cfg="${LOA_REPO_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}}/.loa.config.yaml" content="" l in_blk=0

+    case "$l" in
+      destructive_command_guard:*) in_blk=1; continue ;;
+      [A-Za-z_]*) in_blk=0; continue ;;
+    esac

+# Exported entry points (source with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1).
+_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class() {
+  local LC_ALL=C
+  _bdb_heredoc_scrub "${1:-}" >/dev/null

+heredoc_nonexec() {
+  [[ "$(_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]

+# Library mode: only when SOURCED. Executed with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 the hook runs

+    case "${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}" in
+      '('|')'|'{'|'}'|do|done|then|else|elif|if|fi|while|until|for|case|esac|select|function|coproc) return 0 ;;
+    esac

+# _bdb_hd_header <line> — parse one header line. Sets _hd_ops (heredoc count,
+# -1 = unreadable), _hd_delim, _hd_quoted, _hd_tabs, _hd_cls, _hd_dests[],
+# _hd_pipe (pipeline id of the heredoc on this line).
+_bdb_hd_header() {
+  local line="${1:-}" k nt t opi=-1 w seg=0 pipe=0
+  local -a tpipe mtoks
+  _hd_ops=0 _hd_delim="" _hd_quoted=0 _hd_tabs=0 _hd_cls=none _hd_pipe=-1
+  _hd_dests=()
+  if ! _bdb_hd_tokenize "$line"; then _hd_ops=-1; return; fi
+  nt=${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}
+  tpipe=()
+  for ((k = 0; k < nt; k++)); do
+    t="${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}"
+    case "$t" in
+      ';'|';;'|'&'|'&&'|'||'|'('|')') pipe=$((pipe + 1)); tpipe[k]=-1; continue ;;
+      '|'|'|&') tpipe[k]=-1; continue ;;
+    esac

+  fi
+  _hd_pipe="${tpipe[opi]}"

+  _bdb_hd_tokenize "$line"    # _bdb_hd_ctx_bad reused the token buffer
+  # Classify every member of the heredoc's pipeline; the most executing wins.
+  local cls=nonexec
+  k=0

+    if [[ "${tpipe[k]}" != "$_hd_pipe" ]]; then k=$((k + 1)); continue; fi

+# _bdb_hd_segword <segment> → _hd_w (command word after wrapper stripping,
+# quotes and an absolute path removed) and _hd_rest (the text after it).
+_bdb_hd_segword() {
+  local s="${1:-}" w guard=0
+  _hd_w="" _hd_rest=""

+    guard=$((guard + 1))
+    s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"

+      '('|'{'|'!'|'\'|'"'|"'") s="${s:1}"; continue ;;
+    esac
+    w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"

+    case "$w" in
+      sudo|doas|command|exec|env|nice|time|nohup|builtin|stdbuf|ionice)

+          s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"

+            -S|-S[[:space:]]*|--split-string*) _hd_w="sh"; _hd_rest="$s"; return ;;
+            -[ugnCphUrtTDc]|-[ugnCphUrtTDc][[:space:]]*)

+            *) break ;;

+# _bdb_hd_scan_body <first> <last> <quoted> — per-segment scan of
+# _bdb_hd_L[first..last]. Sets _hd_kept (fence-verb segments, one per line),

+# _hd_full (1 = the body needs the full scan).
+_bdb_hd_scan_body() {

+      seg="${t%%$'\n'*}"
+      _bdb_hd_segword "$seg"

+        if [[ "$_hd_w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_varw ]]; then
+          _hd_full=1
+          _hd_synth="${_hd_synth}rm${_hd_rest}"$'\n'"git${_hd_rest}"$'\n'"kubectl${_hd_rest}"$'\n'
+        elif _bdb_hd_is_destructive "$_hd_w"; then
+          _hd_kept="${_hd_kept}${_hd_w}${_hd_rest}"$'\n'
+        elif _bdb_hd_is_interp "$_hd_w" || _bdb_hd_is_runner "$_hd_w"; then
+          _hd_full=1
+        fi
+      fi
+      [[ "$t" == *$'\n'* ]] || break
+      t="${t#*$'\n'}"
+    done
+  done
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_same_line_exec <basename> <header idx> <body first> <body last>
+# → 0 when the target is named anywhere else in the command outside a safe
+# reader (it may be executed, sourced, made executable, copied or moved).
+_bdb_hd_same_line_exec() {
+  local b="$1" hi="$2" bf="$3" bl="$4" k nt t u c cw seg_has pipe start j own
+  for ((k = 0; k < _bdb_hd_n; k++)); do
+    (( k >= bf && k <= bl )) && continue

+      t="${_bdb_hd_tok[j]:-}"
+      if (( j < nt )) && ! [[ "$t" =~ ^(';'|';;'|'&'|'&&'|'||'|'('|')'|'|'|'|&')$ ]]; then continue; fi

+    fi

+    (( ctx )) && cls=interpreter

+# The #1245 header grammar (byte-identical to _bdb_scrub_cat_heredoc's).

+    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.status | st) else null end) as $cst
+    | {cycle: $cycle, derived_at: $ts, stale_hours: ($win / 3600), file_authoritative: ($fa == 1),
+       state: $s, cache_state: $cs, cache_status: $cst,
+       cache: (if $cache_ok == 0 then "unparseable" elif $c == null then "missing" else "present" end),

+cmd_record_round() {

+  p=$(fb_parse "$file" "$gate")

+    echo "recorded: $gate APPROVED — breaker counters unchanged"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
+              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
+              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
+              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
+              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
+  ts=$(now_iso); now=$(date +%s)
+  atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson p "$p" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$ts" --argjson now "$now" \
+      --arg gate "$gate" --arg sprint "$sprint" "$JQ_DEFS"'
+    (if type == "object" and (.triggers | type) == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
+    | ($p.counts | tojson) as $c
+    | (if $p.hash != "none" and $p.hash == (.triggers.same_issue.last_hash // null)
+       then .triggers.same_issue.count = ((.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) + 1)
+       else .triggers.same_issue.count = 1 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $p.hash end)
+    | (if (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts // null) != null and .triggers.no_progress.last_counts == $c
+       then .triggers.no_progress.count = ((.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) + 1)
+       else .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 end)
+    | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $c
+    | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ((.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) + 1)
+    | (.triggers.timeout.started // null | epoch) as $start
+    | ( if .triggers.same_issue.count >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
+          then ["same_issue", "same issue hash \($p.hash[0:8]) seen \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times in a row"]
+        elif .triggers.no_progress.count >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
+          then ["no_progress", "finding counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds"]
+        elif .triggers.cycle_count.current >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
+          then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds reached the limit \(.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)"]
+        elif $start != null and ($now - $start) >= ((.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) * 3600)
+          then ["timeout", "run older than \(.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) hours"]
+        elif (.state // "CLOSED") == "OPEN" then ["open", "breaker already OPEN"]
+        else null end ) as $trip
+    | .last_round = {gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end), verdict: $p.verdict, hash: $p.hash, ts: $ts}
+    | if $trip != null and $trip[0] != "open" and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
+      then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end)}])
+      elif $trip != null then .state = "OPEN"
+      else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end
+    | .last_trip = $trip' || return 3
+  trip=$(jq -r '.last_trip // empty | if type == "array" then "\(.[0]): \(.[1])" else empty end' "$breaker")
+  out=$(jq -r '"recorded: \(.last_round.gate) \(.last_round.verdict // "no verdict") — cycle \(.triggers.cycle_count.current)/\(.triggers.cycle_count.limit), same_issue \(.triggers.same_issue.count)/\(.triggers.same_issue.threshold), no_progress \(.triggers.no_progress.count)/\(.triggers.no_progress.threshold)"' "$breaker")
+  echo "$out"
+  if [[ -n "$trip" ]]; then
+    atomic_update "$state_file" --arg ts "$ts" '.state = "HALTED"' || return 3
+    echo "TRIPPED: $trip"
+    return 10
+  fi
+  return 0
+}

+cmd_mark() {
+  [[ -n "$skill" && -n "$sprint" ]] || usage
+  mkdir -p "$run_dir"
+  atomic_update "$run_dir/implement-active.json" --arg k "$skill" --arg s "$sprint" --arg ts "$(now_iso)" \
+    '{skill: $k, sprint: $s, started_at: $ts}' || return 3

+  fi

+}

+      report=$(jq -c --arg w "$why" '.notes += [$w]' <<<"$report")
+    fi
+  fi

+  if (( json )); then
+    jq . <<<"$report"
+  else
+    jq -r '"derive: files say \(.state), cache said \(.cache_state // "nothing") (\(if .drift then "drift" else "in sync" end))"
+           + (if .written then " — caches rewritten" else "" end), (.notes[] | "  note: " + .)' <<<"$report"
+  fi
+  return 0
+}

+cmd_record_round() {
+  [[ -n "$gate" && -n "$file" ]] || usage
+  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: record-round: no feedback file at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
+  local p th ts now out trip
+  p=$(fb_parse "$file" "$gate")
+  if [[ "$(jq -r '.approved' <<<"$p")" == true ]]; then
+    echo "recorded: $gate APPROVED — breaker counters unchanged"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
+              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
+              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
+              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
+              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
+  ts=$(now_iso); now=$(date +%s)
+  atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson p "$p" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$ts" --argjson now "$now" \
+      --arg gate "$gate" --arg sprint "$sprint" "$JQ_DEFS"'

+    | ($p.counts | tojson) as $c
+    | (if $p.hash != "none" and $p.hash == (.triggers.same_issue.last_hash // null)
+       then .triggers.same_issue.count = ((.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) + 1)
+       else .triggers.same_issue.count = 1 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $p.hash end)
+    | (if (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts // null) != null and .triggers.no_progress.last_counts == $c
+       then .triggers.no_progress.count = ((.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) + 1)
+       else .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 end)
+    | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $c
+    | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ((.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) + 1)
+    | (.triggers.timeout.started // null | epoch) as $start
+    | ( if .triggers.same_issue.count >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
+          then ["same_issue", "same issue hash \($p.hash[0:8]) seen \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times in a row"]
+        elif .triggers.no_progress.count >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
+          then ["no_progress", "finding counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds"]
+        elif .triggers.cycle_count.current >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
+          then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds reached the limit \(.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)"]
+        elif $start != null and ($now - $start) >= ((.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) * 3600)
+          then ["timeout", "run older than \(.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) hours"]
+        elif (.state // "CLOSED") == "OPEN" then ["open", "breaker already OPEN"]
+        else null end ) as $trip
+    | .last_round = {gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end), verdict: $p.verdict, hash: $p.hash, ts: $ts}
+    | if $trip != null and $trip[0] != "open" and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
+      then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end)}])
+      elif $trip != null then .state = "OPEN"
+      else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end
+    | .last_trip = $trip' || return 3
+  trip=$(jq -r '.last_trip // empty | if type == "array" then "\(.[0]): \(.[1])" else empty end' "$breaker")
+  out=$(jq -r '"recorded: \(.last_round.gate) \(.last_round.verdict // "no verdict") — cycle \(.triggers.cycle_count.current)/\(.triggers.cycle_count.limit), same_issue \(.triggers.same_issue.count)/\(.triggers.same_issue.threshold), no_progress \(.triggers.no_progress.count)/\(.triggers.no_progress.threshold)"' "$breaker")
+  echo "$out"
+  if [[ -n "$trip" ]]; then
+    atomic_update "$state_file" --arg ts "$ts" '.state = "HALTED"' || return 3
+    echo "TRIPPED: $trip"
+    return 10
+  fi
+  return 0
+}
+
+cmd_mark() {
+  [[ -n "$skill" && -n "$sprint" ]] || usage
+  mkdir -p "$run_dir"

+    '{skill: $k, sprint: $s, started_at: $ts}' || return 3
+  if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
+    local err drc=0
+    err=$( { write=1; json=0; cmd_derive >/dev/null; } 2>&1 ) || drc=$?
+    if (( drc != 0 && drc != 4 )); then printf '%s\n' "$err" >&2; fi
+  fi
+  echo "marked: $skill $sprint ($run_dir/implement-active.json)"
+}
+
 case "$sub" in
-  write) cmd_write ;;
-  read)  cmd_read ;;
+  write)  cmd_write ;;
+  read)   cmd_read ;;
+  derive) cmd_derive ;;
+  record-round) cmd_record_round ;;
+  mark)   cmd_mark ;;
+  unmark) rm -f -- "$run_dir/implement-active.json" "$run_dir/implement-active.json.lock"; echo "unmarked" ;;
   *) usage ;;
 esac

+        gate_cell "$ROOT/src/x.ts" plain ""
+        [ "$(decision3)" = ask ] || { echo "$body: expected ask" >&2; return 1; }

+    done

+    [ "$(decision3)" = ask ]
+}
+
+@test "IG-33 a RUNNING state.json whose derived_at is older than run_mode.stale_hours does not sanction; run_mode.stale_hours narrows the window" {
+    command -v yq >/dev/null || skip "yq not installed"

+    jq -nc '{state: "RUNNING", derived_at: (now - 3 * 3600 | floor | todate), timestamps: {last_activity: (now | floor | todate)}}' > "$ROOT/.run/state.json"
+    gate_cell "$ROOT/src/x.ts" plain ""
+    [ "$(decision3)" = ask ]
+    jq -nc '{state: "RUNNING", derived_at: (now - 3600 | floor | todate), timestamps: {last_activity: (now | floor | todate)}}' > "$ROOT/.run/state.json"
+    gate_cell "$ROOT/src/x.ts" plain ""
+    [ "$(decision3)" = allow ]
+    # a sprint-plan cache derived 3 h ago is stale under stale_hours: 2 → deny falls back to ask
+    rm -f "$ROOT/.run/state.json"
+    printf 'implement_gate:\n  mode: deny\nrun_mode:\n  stale_hours: 2\n' > "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
+    jq -nc '{plan_id: "p", state: "COMPLETE", derived_at: (now - 3 * 3600 | floor | todate), timestamps: {last_activity: (now | floor | todate)}}' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"
+    rm -f "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl"
+    gate_cell "$ROOT/src/x.ts" plain ""
+    [ "$(decision3)" = ask ]
+    run jq -r '.decision' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl"
+    [ "$output" = unknown_position ]
 }

@@ -0,0 +1,197 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/karpathy-surgical-diff.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.3
+# (AC-2.3; PRD AC-4.3; SDD D-4.3, D-4.2a; DEC-0141)
+#
+# The surgical-diff hook keys its running total on the checkpoint task
+# (`run-checkpoint.sh read --json`), else the sprint, else the session id;
+# keeps one sanitised file per task under the state directory (at most 20);
+# deletes the legacy session-long file; writes the summary the review's
+# SURGICAL axis reads; and is silent when the knob is off. A fixture
+# checkpoint (LOA_RUN_DIR) and a fake `br` on PATH stand in for a live run.
+# =============================================================================
+
+bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
+
+setup() {
+    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
+    HOOK="$R/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh"
+    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not available"
+    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not available"
+    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
+    export LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$T/config.yaml"
+    export KARPATHY_STATE_DIR="$T/state"
+    export KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE="$T/summary.json"
+    export KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE="$T/karpathy-task-state.jsonl"
+    export KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR="$T/trajectory"
+    export LOA_RUN_DIR="$T/run"
+    unset LOA_SESSION_ID LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE
+    mkdir -p "$T/run" "$T/bin"
+    printf 'karpathy_principles:\n  surgical_diff_warning: true\n  diff_lines_per_task: 5\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
+    # Fake beads: every bead reports closed unless BR_STATUS says otherwise.
+    printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'printf "{\"status\":\"%s\"}\n" "${BR_STATUS:-closed}"' > "$T/bin/br"
+    chmod +x "$T/bin/br"
+    export PATH="$T/bin:$PATH"
+}
+
+# checkpoint <sprint> [task] — a schema-2 run state with that checkpoint
+checkpoint() {
+    jq -n --arg s "$1" --arg t "${2:-}" \
+        '{schema_version: 2, state: "RUNNING",
+          checkpoint: {sprint: $s, task: (if $t == "" then null else $t end), phase: "IMPLEMENT", ts: "2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"}}' \
+        > "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json"
+}
+
+# write_lines <n> [session_id] — one Write payload adding n lines
+write_lines() {
+    local n="$1" sid="${2:-sess-1}" content
+    content=$(seq 1 "$n" | paste -sd'\n' -)
+    jq -nc --arg c "$content" --arg s "$sid" \
+        '{tool_name: "Write", session_id: $s, tool_input: {file_path: "/repo/src/x.sh", content: $c}}' \
+        | bash "$HOOK"
+}
+
+@test "KS-1 the counter resets when the checkpoint task changes" {
+    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-aaa
+    write_lines 3
+    write_lines 2
+    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "bd-aaa" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "5" ]
+    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-bbb
+    write_lines 2
+    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "bd-bbb" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "2" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.over' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "false" ]
+    [ "$(wc -l < "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-aaa.jsonl")" -eq 2 ]
+    [ "$(wc -l < "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-bbb.jsonl")" -eq 1 ]
+    [ "$(tail -1 "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-aaa.jsonl" | jq -r '.running_total')" = "5" ]
+}
+
+@test "KS-2 with no run in progress the key is the payload's session id, then LOA_SESSION_ID" {
+    write_lines 1 "abc-123"
+    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/abc-123.jsonl" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "abc-123" ]
+    jq -nc '{tool_name: "Edit", tool_input: {file_path: "/repo/a", old_string: "", new_string: "x\ny"}}' \
+        | LOA_SESSION_ID=env-sess bash "$HOOK"
+    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/env-sess.jsonl" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "2" ]
+}
+
+@test "KS-3 a checkpoint whose task is still open in beads keys on the sprint" {
+    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-open
+    BR_STATUS=open write_lines 2
+    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/sprint-256.jsonl" ]
+    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-open.jsonl" ]
+    # A sprint-granularity checkpoint (no task) keys on the sprint too.
+    checkpoint sprint-257
+    write_lines 1
+    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "sprint-257" ]
+}
+
+@test "KS-4 the summary carries exactly task, lines, threshold, over, updated_at after each write" {
+    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-sum
+    write_lines 4
+    run jq -c 'keys' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE"
+    [ "$output" = '["lines","over","task","threshold","updated_at"]' ]
+    jq -e '.task == "bd-sum" and .lines == 4 and .threshold == 5 and .over == false
+           and (.updated_at | test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:]{8}Z$"))' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE" >/dev/null
+    run --separate-stderr write_lines 3
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    jq -e '.lines == 7 and .over == true' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE" >/dev/null
+    # The stderr warning keeps its wording.
+    [[ "$stderr" == "[karpathy-surgical-warn] Session diff total 7 lines exceeds threshold 5. Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes): verify every changed line traces to the stated task. State: $KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-sum.jsonl" ]]
+    ls "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE".tmp.* >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 1
+    true
+}
+
+@test "KS-5 the state directory keeps the 20 most recently written task files" {
+    mkdir -p "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR"
+    local i
+    for i in $(seq -w 1 25); do
+        echo '{"lines_changed":1}' > "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-old-$i.jsonl"
+        touch -d "2026-01-01 00:00:$i" "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-old-$i.jsonl"
+    done
+    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-new
+    write_lines 1
+    [ "$(ls "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR"/*.jsonl | wc -l)" -eq 20 ]
+    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-new.jsonl" ]
+    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-old-25.jsonl" ]
+    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-old-06.jsonl" ]
+    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-old-01.jsonl" ]
+}
+
+@test "KS-6 the legacy session-long state file is deleted on the first run" {
+    printf '{"lines_changed":900,"running_total":900}\n' > "$KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE"
+    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-leg
+    write_lines 1
+    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE" ]
+    # The legacy total does not leak into the new layout.
+    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "1" ]
+}
+
+@test "KS-7 task names are sanitised to ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\$ and stay inside the state directory" {
+    checkpoint sprint-256 'bd-1'
+    jq '.checkpoint.task = "Task 2.3: ../../evil\nname"' "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json" > "$T/s" && mv "$T/s" "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json"
+    write_lines 1
+    run ls -A "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR"
+    [ "${#lines[@]}" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "${lines[0]}" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\.jsonl$ ]]
+    [ "${lines[0]}" = "Task_2.3__.._.._evil_name.jsonl" ]
+    [ "$(find "$T" -name '*evil*' | wc -l)" -eq 1 ]
+    # A leading dot cannot make a hidden (unrotated) file.
+    jq '.checkpoint.task = ".hidden"' "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json" > "$T/s" && mv "$T/s" "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json"
+    write_lines 1
+    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/_hidden.jsonl" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "_hidden" ]
+}
+
+@test "KS-8 knob off is silent: no state, no summary, no stderr" {
+    printf 'karpathy_principles:\n  surgical_diff_warning: false\n  diff_lines_per_task: 1\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
+    printf 'x\n' > "$KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE"
+    run --separate-stderr write_lines 9
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ -z "$output" ] && [ -z "$stderr" ]
+    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR" ] && [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE" ]
+    # The `lean` profile turns it off without the key; an explicit true wins over lean.
+    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\nkarpathy_principles:\n  diff_lines_per_task: 1\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
+    run --separate-stderr write_lines 9
+    [ -z "$stderr" ] && [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE" ]
+    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\nkarpathy_principles:\n  surgical_diff_warning: true\n  diff_lines_per_task: 1\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
+    run --separate-stderr write_lines 9
+    [[ "$stderr" == *"[karpathy-surgical-warn]"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "KS-9 content never reaches state, summary or trajectory" {
+    local REDACTED-TEST-SECRET"
+    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-sec
+    jq -nc --arg c "a
+$secret
+b
+c
+d
+e" '{tool_name: "Write", session_id: "s", tool_input: {file_path: "/repo/x", content: $c}}' | bash "$HOOK" 2>/dev/null
+    ! grep -rqF "$secret" "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR" "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE" "$KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR"
+    [ -f "$KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR/karpathy-$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d).jsonl" ]
+}
+
+@test "KS-10 a symlinked state directory or task file is not written through" {
+    mkdir -p "$T/elsewhere"
+    ln -s "$T/elsewhere" "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR"
+    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-link
+    write_lines 1
+    [ -z "$(ls -A "$T/elsewhere")" ]
+    rm "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR"; mkdir -p "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR"
+    ln -s "$T/elsewhere/target" "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-link.jsonl"
+    write_lines 1
+    [ ! -e "$T/elsewhere/target" ]
+}
+
+@test "KS-11 malformed or foreign payloads are a silent no-op" {
+    run bash -c "printf 'not json' | '$HOOK'"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    run bash -c "printf '%s' '{\"tool_name\":\"Bash\",\"tool_input\":{\"command\":\"ls\"}}' | '$HOOK'"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    run bash -c "printf '%s' '[1,2]' | '$HOOK'"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR" ]
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,136 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/lint-invariants.bats — cycle-129 D-4.5 (AC-2.5)
+#
+# The five C-TEAM rows left constraints.json; generate-constraints.sh omits the
+# "## Agent Teams" table when the class is empty and renders it when rows
+# exist; lint-invariants.sh fails when the kernel and the registry disagree.
+# The generator runs against a fixture tree (it resolves its inputs relative
+# to the working directory), never against the live kernel.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
+    GEN="$R/.claude/scripts/generate-constraints.sh"
+    LINT="$R/.claude/scripts/lint-invariants.sh"
+    F="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/tree"
+    mkdir -p "$F/.claude/loa" "$F/.claude/data" "$F/.claude/templates"
+    cp -R "$R/.claude/templates/constraints" "$F/.claude/templates/constraints"
+    cp "$R/.claude/data/constraints.json" "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json"
+    cp "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+}
+
+# A kernel that still carries the pre-cycle-129 Agent Teams block, placed
+# between the merge constraints and the Agent-Network section as it was.
+add_team_block() {
+    python3 -I - "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" <<'PY'
+import sys
+p = sys.argv[1]
+s = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
+anchor = "## Agent-Network Primitives"
+block = ("## Agent Teams\n\n| Rule | Why |\n|------|-----|\n"
+         "<!-- @constraint-generated: start agent_teams_constraints | hash:0000000000000000 -->\n"
+         "<!-- DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/constraints.json -->\n"
+         "| MUST stale row | stale |\n"
+         "<!-- @constraint-generated: end agent_teams_constraints -->\n\n")
+assert s.count(anchor) == 1
+open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s.replace(anchor, block + anchor))
+PY
+}
+
+add_team_row() {
+    jq '.constraints += [{"id":"C-TEAM-901","name":"fixture_row","category":"agent_teams","rule_type":"MUST",
+        "text":"fixture rule","text_variants":{"claude-loa-md":"MUST fixture rule"},"why":"fixture why","order":0,
+        "layers":[{"target":"claude-loa-md","section":"agent_teams_constraints","render_as":"table_row"}],
+        "severity":"low","source_incident":"#0"}]' "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json" > "$F/c.json"
+    mv "$F/c.json" "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json"
+}
+
+gen() { (cd "$F" && bash "$GEN" --section "${1:-agent_teams_constraints}"); }
+
+@test "LI-1 constraints.json carries no C-TEAM rows and no agent_teams_constraints layer" {
+    run jq '[.constraints[] | select((.id | startswith("C-TEAM")) or any(.layers[]?; .section == "agent_teams_constraints"))] | length' \
+        "$R/.claude/data/constraints.json"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ "$output" = "0" ]
+}
+

index 00000000..cec31272
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/unit/karpathy-surgical-diff.bats
@@ -0,0 +1,197 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/karpathy-surgical-diff.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.3
+# (AC-2.3; PRD AC-4.3; SDD D-4.3, D-4.2a; DEC-0141)
+#
+# The surgical-diff hook keys its running total on the checkpoint task
+# (`run-checkpoint.sh read --json`), else the sprint, else the session id;
+# keeps one sanitised file per task under the state directory (at most 20);
+# deletes the legacy session-long file; writes the summary the review's
+# SURGICAL axis reads; and is silent when the knob is off. A fixture
+# checkpoint (LOA_RUN_DIR) and a fake `br` on PATH stand in for a live run.
+# =============================================================================
+
+bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
+
+setup() {
+    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
+    HOOK="$R/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh"
+    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not available"
+    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not available"
+    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
+    export LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$T/config.yaml"
+    export KARPATHY_STATE_DIR="$T/state"
+    export KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE="$T/summary.json"
+    export KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE="$T/karpathy-task-state.jsonl"
+    export KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR="$T/trajectory"
+    export LOA_RUN_DIR="$T/run"
+    unset LOA_SESSION_ID LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE
+    mkdir -p "$T/run" "$T/bin"
+    printf 'karpathy_principles:\n  surgical_diff_warning: true\n  diff_lines_per_task: 5\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
+    # Fake beads: every bead reports closed unless BR_STATUS says otherwise.
+    printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'printf "{\"status\":\"%s\"}\n" "${BR_STATUS:-closed}"' > "$T/bin/br"
+    chmod +x "$T/bin/br"
+    export PATH="$T/bin:$PATH"
+}
+
+# checkpoint <sprint> [task] — a schema-2 run state with that checkpoint
+checkpoint() {
+    jq -n --arg s "$1" --arg t "${2:-}" \
+        '{schema_version: 2, state: "RUNNING",
+          checkpoint: {sprint: $s, task: (if $t == "" then null else $t end), phase: "IMPLEMENT", ts: "2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"}}' \
+        > "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json"
+}
+
+# write_lines <n> [session_id] — one Write payload adding n lines
+write_lines() {
+    local n="$1" sid="${2:-sess-1}" content
+    content=$(seq 1 "$n" | paste -sd'\n' -)
+    jq -nc --arg c "$content" --arg s "$sid" \
+        '{tool_name: "Write", session_id: $s, tool_input: {file_path: "/repo/src/x.sh", content: $c}}' \
+        | bash "$HOOK"
+}
+
+@test "KS-1 the counter resets when the checkpoint task changes" {
+    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-aaa
+    write_lines 3
+    write_lines 2
+    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "bd-aaa" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "5" ]
+    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-bbb
+    write_lines 2
+    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "bd-bbb" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "2" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.over' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "false" ]
+    [ "$(wc -l < "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-aaa.jsonl")" -eq 2 ]
+    [ "$(wc -l < "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-bbb.jsonl")" -eq 1 ]
+    [ "$(tail -1 "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-aaa.jsonl" | jq -r '.running_total')" = "5" ]
+}
+
+@test "KS-2 with no run in progress the key is the payload's session id, then LOA_SESSION_ID" {
+    write_lines 1 "abc-123"
+    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/abc-123.jsonl" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "abc-123" ]
+    jq -nc '{tool_name: "Edit", tool_input: {file_path: "/repo/a", old_string: "", new_string: "x\ny"}}' \
+        | LOA_SESSION_ID=env-sess bash "$HOOK"
+    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/env-sess.jsonl" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "2" ]
+}
+
+@test "KS-3 a checkpoint whose task is still open in beads keys on the sprint" {
+    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-open
+    BR_STATUS=open write_lines 2
+    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/sprint-256.jsonl" ]
+    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-open.jsonl" ]
+    # A sprint-granularity checkpoint (no task) keys on the sprint too.
+    checkpoint sprint-257
+    write_lines 1
+    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "sprint-257" ]
+}
+
+@test "KS-4 the summary carries exactly task, lines, threshold, over, updated_at after each write" {
+    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-sum
+    write_lines 4
+    run jq -c 'keys' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE"
+    [ "$output" = '["lines","over","task","threshold","updated_at"]' ]
+    jq -e '.task == "bd-sum" and .lines == 4 and .threshold == 5 and .over == false
+           and (.updated_at | test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:]{8}Z$"))' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE" >/dev/null
+    run --separate-stderr write_lines 3
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    jq -e '.lines == 7 and .over == true' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE" >/dev/null
+    # The stderr warning keeps its wording.
+    [[ "$stderr" == "[karpathy-surgical-warn] Session diff total 7 lines exceeds threshold 5. Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes): verify every changed line traces to the stated task. State: $KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-sum.jsonl" ]]
+    ls "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE".tmp.* >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 1
+    true
+}
+
+@test "KS-5 the state directory keeps the 20 most recently written task files" {
+    mkdir -p "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR"
+    local i
+    for i in $(seq -w 1 25); do
+        echo '{"lines_changed":1}' > "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-old-$i.jsonl"
+        touch -d "2026-01-01 00:00:$i" "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-old-$i.jsonl"
+    done
+    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-new
+    write_lines 1
+    [ "$(ls "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR"/*.jsonl | wc -l)" -eq 20 ]
+    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-new.jsonl" ]
+    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-old-25.jsonl" ]
+    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-old-06.jsonl" ]
+    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-old-01.jsonl" ]
+}
+
+@test "KS-6 the legacy session-long state file is deleted on the first run" {
+    printf '{"lines_changed":900,"running_total":900}\n' > "$KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE"
+    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-leg
+    write_lines 1
+    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE" ]
+    # The legacy total does not leak into the new layout.
+    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "1" ]
+}
+
+@test "KS-7 task names are sanitised to ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\$ and stay inside the state directory" {
+    checkpoint sprint-256 'bd-1'
+    jq '.checkpoint.task = "Task 2.3: ../../evil\nname"' "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json" > "$T/s" && mv "$T/s" "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json"
+    write_lines 1
+    run ls -A "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR"
+    [ "${#lines[@]}" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "${lines[0]}" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\.jsonl$ ]]
+    [ "${lines[0]}" = "Task_2.3__.._.._evil_name.jsonl" ]
+    [ "$(find "$T" -name '*evil*' | wc -l)" -eq 1 ]
+    # A leading dot cannot make a hidden (unrotated) file.
+    jq '.checkpoint.task = ".hidden"' "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json" > "$T/s" && mv "$T/s" "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json"
+    write_lines 1
+    [ -f "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/_hidden.jsonl" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "_hidden" ]
+}
+
+@test "KS-8 knob off is silent: no state, no summary, no stderr" {
+    printf 'karpathy_principles:\n  surgical_diff_warning: false\n  diff_lines_per_task: 1\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
+    printf 'x\n' > "$KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE"
+    run --separate-stderr write_lines 9
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ -z "$output" ] && [ -z "$stderr" ]
+    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR" ] && [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE" ]
+    # The `lean` profile turns it off without the key; an explicit true wins over lean.
+    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\nkarpathy_principles:\n  diff_lines_per_task: 1\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
+    run --separate-stderr write_lines 9
+    [ -z "$stderr" ] && [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE" ]
+    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\nkarpathy_principles:\n  surgical_diff_warning: true\n  diff_lines_per_task: 1\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
+    run --separate-stderr write_lines 9
+    [[ "$stderr" == *"[karpathy-surgical-warn]"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "KS-9 content never reaches state, summary or trajectory" {
+    local REDACTED-TEST-SECRET"
+    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-sec
+    jq -nc --arg c "a
+$secret
+b
+c
+d
+e" '{tool_name: "Write", session_id: "s", tool_input: {file_path: "/repo/x", content: $c}}' | bash "$HOOK" 2>/dev/null
+    ! grep -rqF "$secret" "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR" "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE" "$KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR"
+    [ -f "$KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR/karpathy-$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d).jsonl" ]
+}
+
+@test "KS-10 a symlinked state directory or task file is not written through" {
+    mkdir -p "$T/elsewhere"
+    ln -s "$T/elsewhere" "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR"
+    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-link
+    write_lines 1
+    [ -z "$(ls -A "$T/elsewhere")" ]
+    rm "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR"; mkdir -p "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR"
+    ln -s "$T/elsewhere/target" "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/bd-link.jsonl"
+    write_lines 1
+    [ ! -e "$T/elsewhere/target" ]
+}
+
+@test "KS-11 malformed or foreign payloads are a silent no-op" {
+    run bash -c "printf 'not json' | '$HOOK'"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    run bash -c "printf '%s' '{\"tool_name\":\"Bash\",\"tool_input\":{\"command\":\"ls\"}}' | '$HOOK'"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    run bash -c "printf '%s' '[1,2]' | '$HOOK'"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ ! -e "$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR" ]
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/lint-invariants.bats — cycle-129 D-4.5 (AC-2.5)
+#
+# The five C-TEAM rows left constraints.json; generate-constraints.sh omits the
+# "## Agent Teams" table when the class is empty and renders it when rows
+# exist; lint-invariants.sh fails when the kernel and the registry disagree.
+# The generator runs against a fixture tree (it resolves its inputs relative
+# to the working directory), never against the live kernel.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
+    GEN="$R/.claude/scripts/generate-constraints.sh"
+    LINT="$R/.claude/scripts/lint-invariants.sh"
+    F="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/tree"
+    mkdir -p "$F/.claude/loa" "$F/.claude/data" "$F/.claude/templates"
+    cp -R "$R/.claude/templates/constraints" "$F/.claude/templates/constraints"
+    cp "$R/.claude/data/constraints.json" "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json"
+    cp "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+}
+
+# A kernel that still carries the pre-cycle-129 Agent Teams block, placed
+# between the merge constraints and the Agent-Network section as it was.
+add_team_block() {
+    python3 -I - "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" <<'PY'
+import sys
+p = sys.argv[1]
+s = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
+anchor = "## Agent-Network Primitives"
+block = ("## Agent Teams\n\n| Rule | Why |\n|------|-----|\n"
+         "<!-- @constraint-generated: start agent_teams_constraints | hash:0000000000000000 -->\n"
+         "<!-- DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/constraints.json -->\n"
+         "| MUST stale row | stale |\n"
+         "<!-- @constraint-generated: end agent_teams_constraints -->\n\n")
+assert s.count(anchor) == 1
+open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s.replace(anchor, block + anchor))
+PY
+}
+
+add_team_row() {
+    jq '.constraints += [{"id":"C-TEAM-901","name":"fixture_row","category":"agent_teams","rule_type":"MUST",
+        "text":"fixture rule","text_variants":{"claude-loa-md":"MUST fixture rule"},"why":"fixture why","order":0,
+        "layers":[{"target":"claude-loa-md","section":"agent_teams_constraints","render_as":"table_row"}],
+        "severity":"low","source_incident":"#0"}]' "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json" > "$F/c.json"
+    mv "$F/c.json" "$F/.claude/data/constraints.json"
+}
+
+gen() { (cd "$F" && bash "$GEN" --section "${1:-agent_teams_constraints}"); }
+
+@test "LI-1 constraints.json carries no C-TEAM rows and no agent_teams_constraints layer" {
+    run jq '[.constraints[] | select((.id | startswith("C-TEAM")) or any(.layers[]?; .section == "agent_teams_constraints"))] | length' \
+        "$R/.claude/data/constraints.json"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ "$output" = "0" ]
+}
+
+@test "LI-2 the live kernel carries neither the Agent Teams heading nor its marker" {
+    ! grep -qxF '## Agent Teams' "$R/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"

+@test "LI-6 rows without the heading block fail loudly and leave the kernel untouched" {

+    cp "$F/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$F/before.md"

@@ -0,0 +1,200 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/profile-floor.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.7 (AC-2.9; PRD
+# AC-9.2; SDD D-9.2, DEC-0166)
+#
+# No profile can reach the floor. The floor source is .claude/data/floor.yaml
+# (read here, never duplicated); its sha256 pin is READ from
+# tests/unit/guard-origins.bats (FLOOR_SHA256) so the two suites cannot
+# disagree. Under `lean` every floor surface reads byte-identically to
+# `standard`: the floor config keys (the two gate skills' flatline_protocol.*
+# config, destructive_command_guard.*, implement_gate.*, hounfour.locality),
+# verdict-derive.sh on fixture feedback files, the adversarial gate's
+# decision and environment, the deny-list file, the fence on the corpus and
+# the FR-1.2b / FR-SZ probes, and user-invoked-commands.txt.
+# =============================================================================
+
+bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
+
+setup() {
+    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
+    LIB="$R/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh"
+    PROFILES="$R/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
+    FLOOR="$R/.claude/data/floor.yaml"
+    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
+    # Two configs that differ ONLY in loa.profile: this repository's own config
+    # (which carries the floor keys it really uses) with the profile set.
+    for p in lean standard; do
+        cp "$R/.loa.config.yaml" "$T/$p.yaml"
+        yq -i ".loa.profile = \"$p\"" "$T/$p.yaml"
+    done
+    unset LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE LOA_PROFILES_FILE
+}
+
+# The floor key patterns, as the lib and the guard register read them.
+floor_keys() { yq -r '.floor_keys[]' "$FLOOR"; }
+
+@test "PF-1 floor.yaml matches the sha256 pin guard-origins.bats carries (one constant, two suites)" {
+    local pin actual
+    pin=$(sed -n 's/^FLOOR_SHA256="\([0-9a-f]\{64\}\)"$/\1/p' "$R/tests/unit/guard-origins.bats")
+    [ -n "$pin" ] || { echo "no FLOOR_SHA256 in guard-origins.bats"; return 1; }
+    actual=$(bash -c 'source "$1/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; sha256_portable "$2"' _ "$R" "$FLOOR" | cut -d' ' -f1)
+    [ "$actual" = "$pin" ] || { echo "floor.yaml sha256 $actual != pinned $pin"; return 1; }
+}
+
+@test "PF-2 no profiles.yaml key matches a floor key or is an ancestor of one" {
+    run python3 -I - "$PROFILES" "$FLOOR" <<'PY'
+import re, subprocess, sys, json
+def load(p):
+    return json.loads(subprocess.check_output(["yq", "-o=json", ".", p]))
+prof, floor = load(sys.argv[1]), load(sys.argv[2])
+keys = sorted({k for v in prof["profiles"].values() for k in v})
+assert len(keys) == 9, keys
+bad = []
+for k in keys:
+    for f in floor["floor_keys"]:
+        rx = "^" + ".+".join(re.escape(s) for s in f.split("*")) + "$"
+        if re.match(rx, k) or f.split("*")[0].startswith(k + "."):
+            bad.append((k, f))
+print("violations:", bad)
+sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
+PY
+    echo "$output"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    # floor_keys_forbidden is not duplicated into profiles.yaml.
+    [ "$(yq -r 'has("floor_keys_forbidden")' "$PROFILES")" = "false" ]
+}
+
+@test "PF-3 under lean the resolved document names no floor key and every floor key reads as under standard" {
+    local p k
+    for p in lean standard; do
+        LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" bash "$LIB" json > "$T/$p.json"
+        [ "$(jq -r '.profile' "$T/$p.json")" = "$p" ]
+    done
+    # Concrete floor keys: every leaf path of this config and the example that a
+    # floor pattern matches (flatline_protocol.*.companion_voice expands here).
+    yq -o=json '.' "$R/.loa.config.yaml" > "$T/cfg.json"
+    yq -o=json '.' "$R/.loa.config.yaml.example" > "$T/ex.json"
+    floor_keys > "$T/floor.txt"
+    python3 -I - "$T/cfg.json" "$T/ex.json" "$T/floor.txt" > "$T/concrete.txt" <<'PY'
+import json, re, sys
+pats = [l.strip() for l in open(sys.argv[3]) if l.strip()]
+rxs = ["^" + ".+".join(re.escape(s) for s in p.split("*")) + "$" for p in pats]
+out = set(p for p in pats if "*" not in p)
+def walk(x, path):
+    if isinstance(x, dict):
+        for k, v in x.items():
+            walk(v, path + [str(k)])
+    if path:
+        key = ".".join(path)
+        if any(re.match(r, key) for r in rxs):
+            out.add(key)
+for f in sys.argv[1:3]:
+    walk(json.load(open(f)), [])
+print("\n".join(sorted(k for k in out if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*", k))))
+PY
+    grep -qx 'flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled' "$T/concrete.txt"
+    grep -qx 'flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled' "$T/concrete.txt"
+    grep -q '^flatline_protocol\.[a-z_]*\.companion_voice$' "$T/concrete.txt"
+    while IFS= read -r k; do
+        [ "$(jq -r --arg k "$k" '.knobs | has($k)' "$T/lean.json")" = "false" ] || { echo "lean resolves floor key $k"; return 1; }
+        a=$(LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/lean.yaml" bash "$LIB" knob "$k" __unset__ 2>/dev/null)
+        b=$(LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/standard.yaml" bash "$LIB" knob "$k" __unset__ 2>/dev/null)
+        [ "$a" = "$b" ] || { echo "$k: lean=$a standard=$b"; return 1; }
+    done < "$T/concrete.txt"
+    # The two gate skills' whole flatline_protocol config is byte-identical.
+    for g in code_review security_audit; do
+        cmp <(yq -o=json ".flatline_protocol.$g" "$T/lean.yaml") <(yq -o=json ".flatline_protocol.$g" "$T/standard.yaml")
+    done
+}
+
+@test "PF-4 verdict-derive.sh output is byte-identical under lean and standard" {
+    local f p
+    printf 'All good\n\n## Observations\n\n- **LOW** `a.sh:1` — naming\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":0,"low":1},"sprint_id":"sprint-9","ts":"2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' > "$T/ok.md"
+    printf '## Changes Required\n\n- **HIGH** `a.sh:1` — unchecked input\n\nAll good\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED","counts":{"critical":0,"high":1,"medium":0,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-9","ts":"2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' > "$T/bad.md"
+    for f in ok bad; do
+        for p in lean standard; do
+            rc=0
+            LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" bash "$R/.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh" --file "$T/$f.md" --gate review --json \
+                > "$T/vd-$f-$p.out" 2>&1 || rc=$?
+            echo "$rc" >> "$T/vd-$f-$p.out"
+        done
+        cmp "$T/vd-$f-lean.out" "$T/vd-$f-standard.out"
+    done
+    # The fixtures exercise both outcomes, so identity is not vacuous.
+    ! cmp -s "$T/vd-ok-lean.out" "$T/vd-bad-lean.out"
+}
+
+@test "PF-5 the adversarial-review gate decides identically under lean and standard" {
+    local d="$T/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-999" p rc
+    mkdir -p "$d"
+    for p in lean standard; do
+        yq -i '.flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled = true' "$T/$p.yaml"
+        rc=0
+        printf '{"tool_name":"Write","tool_input":{"file_path":"%s/COMPLETED"}}' "$d" \
+            | env -u LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" LOA_CONFIG_PATH_OVERRIDE="$T/$p.yaml" \
+              bash "$R/.claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh" > "$T/gate-$p.out" 2>&1 || rc=$?
+        echo "$rc" >> "$T/gate-$p.out"
+    done
+    cmp "$T/gate-lean.out" "$T/gate-standard.out"
+    # No dissent envelope for an enabled gate: the gate refuses (exit 2) under both.
+    [ "$(tail -1 "$T/gate-lean.out")" = "2" ]
+    # The gate's environment knob is not a profile key and the gate never sources the lib.
+    ! grep -q 'profile-lib' "$R/.claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh"
+    ! yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | grep -qi 'adversarial'
+}
+
+@test "PF-6 the fence decides every corpus row and the FR-1.2b / FR-SZ probes identically under lean and standard" {
+    local p row cmd rc id
+    jq -r '.id' "$R/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl" > /dev/null
+    # Floor probes (the corpus carries the floor rules named in floor.yaml floor_corpus when they exist).
+    printf '%s\n' \
+        '{"id":"FP-1","cmd":"git stash pop 2>/dev/null"}' \
+        '{"id":"FP-2","cmd":"git stash push -m x | tail -1"}' \
+        '{"id":"FP-3","cmd":"echo x > .claude/hooks/evil.sh"}' \
+        '{"id":"FP-4","cmd":"cp /tmp/a .claude/settings.json"}' \
+        '{"id":"FP-5","cmd":"sed -i s/a/b/ .claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh"}' > "$T/probes.jsonl"
+    cat "$R/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl" "$T/probes.jsonl" > "$T/all.jsonl"
+    for p in lean standard; do
+        mkdir -p "$T/root-$p/repo"
+        cp "$T/$p.yaml" "$T/root-$p/.loa.config.yaml"
+        : > "$T/fence-$p.txt"
+        while IFS= read -r row; do
+            [ -n "$row" ] || continue
+            id=$(jq -r '.id' <<<"$row"); cmd=$(jq -r '.cmd' <<<"$row")
+            rc=0
+            (cd "$T/root-$p/repo" && jq -cn --arg c "$cmd" '{tool_input: {command: $c}}' \
+                | env -u TMPDIR LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 LOA_REPO_ROOT="$T/root-$p" LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" \
+                  bash "$R/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1) || rc=$?
+            echo "$id $rc" >> "$T/fence-$p.txt"
+        done < "$T/all.jsonl"
+    done
+    cmp "$T/fence-lean.txt" "$T/fence-standard.txt"
+    for id in FP-1 FP-2 FP-3 FP-4 FP-5; do
+        grep -qx "$id 2" "$T/fence-lean.txt" || { echo "$id not blocked under lean: $(grep "^$id " "$T/fence-lean.txt")"; return 1; }
+    done
+    # Every floor_corpus row present in the corpus is in the compared set.
+    while IFS= read -r rule; do
+        jq -r --arg r "$rule" 'select(.rule == $r or (($r | endswith("*")) and (.rule | startswith($r | rtrimstr("*"))))) | .id' \
+            "$R/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl" | while IFS= read -r id; do
+            grep -q "^$id " "$T/fence-lean.txt"
+        done
+    done < <(yq -r '.floor_corpus.rules[]' "$FLOOR")
+}
+
+@test "PF-7 the deny list, the System-Zone rules and user-invoked-commands.txt are untouched by resolving any profile" {
+    local f before after p
+    for f in .claude/hooks/settings.deny.json .claude/data/user-invoked-commands.txt .claude/rules/zone-system.md .claude/data/floor.yaml; do
+        before=$(bash -c 'source "$1/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; sha256_portable "$1/$2"' _ "$R" "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)
+        for p in lean standard; do
+            LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE="$T/cache-$p.json" bash "$LIB" json >/dev/null
+        done
+        after=$(bash -c 'source "$1/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; sha256_portable "$1/$2"' _ "$R" "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)
+        [ "$before" = "$after" ]
+    done
+    # The lib reads exactly three inputs and writes only its cache.
+    ! grep -Eq 'settings\.deny|user-invoked-commands|zone-system' "$LIB"
+    # The resolved documents differ only in the profile name and the profile-sourced values.
+    [ "$(jq -r '.profile' "$T/cache-lean.json")" = "lean" ]
+    [ "$(jq -c '.profile_keys' "$T/cache-lean.json")" = "$(jq -c '.profile_keys' "$T/cache-standard.json")" ]
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/profile-lib.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.7 (AC-2.9; PRD
+# AC-9.1, AC-9.3; SDD D-9.1, D-9.3)
+#
+# .claude/data/profiles.yaml + .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh: precedence
+# (explicit key > profile > fallback), every profile defines every key,
+# `standard` equals the oracle captured before any reader changed
+# (tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json), unknown profile, the
+# mtime-keyed cache, the overrides line, the /loa Profile line, the readers
+# that route through loa_knob, and the grep lint for direct reads.
+# =============================================================================
+
+bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
+
+setup() {
+    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
+    LIB="$R/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh"
+    PROFILES="$R/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
+    ORACLE="$R/tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json"
+    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
+    CFG="$T/config.yaml"
+    export LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$CFG"
+    export LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE="$T/run/effective-config.json"
+    : > "$CFG"
+}
+
+knob() { bash "$LIB" knob "$@"; }
+
+@test "PL-1 every profile defines every key, and the key set is the nine optional keys" {
+    run diff <(yq -r '.profiles.lean | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort) <(jq -r '.keys | keys[]' "$ORACLE" | sort)
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    for p in standard full; do
+        run diff <(yq -r ".profiles.$p | keys | .[]" "$PROFILES" | sort) <(yq -r '.profiles.lean | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort)
+        [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    done
+    [ "$(yq -r '.profiles | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort | paste -sd, -)" = "full,lean,standard" ]
+    [ "$(yq -r '.schema_version' "$PROFILES")" = "1" ]
+    ! yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | grep -qx 'interview.pacing'
+}
+
+@test "PL-2 every profile value is a boolean; lean is all false and full all true" {
+    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles[][] | tag] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "!!bool" ]
+    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles.lean[]] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "false" ]
+    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles.full[]] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "true" ]
+}
+
+@test "PL-3 standard equals the oracle captured before any reader changed" {
+    local k want got
+    while IFS= read -r k; do
+        want=$(jq -r --arg k "$k" '.keys[$k].standard' "$ORACLE")
+        got=$(yq -r ".profiles.standard[\"$k\"]" "$PROFILES")
+        [ "$want" = "$got" ] || { echo "standard $k = $got, oracle $want"; return 1; }
+    done < <(jq -r '.keys | keys[]' "$ORACLE")
+    # Outside the two guardrail keys (whose default this cycle changes) the
+    # oracle's standard IS the value the readers returned for the shipped example.
+    run jq -r '.keys | to_entries[] | select(.key | startswith("guardrails.") | not)
+               | select(.value.standard != .value.example_today) | .key' "$ORACLE"
+    [ -z "$output" ]
+    run jq -r '.keys | to_entries[] | select(.key | startswith("guardrails.")) | "\(.value.example_today)/\(.value.standard)"' "$ORACLE"
+    [ "$output" = "$(printf 'true/false\ntrue/false')" ]
+}
+
+@test "PL-4 standard equals the post-cycle example defaults (explicit example value, else the reader's fallback)" {
+    local k ex st
+    while IFS= read -r k; do
+        ex=$(yq -r ".$k" "$R/.loa.config.yaml.example")
+        st=$(yq -r ".profiles.standard[\"$k\"]" "$PROFILES")
+        if [ "$ex" = "null" ]; then
+            ex=$(jq -r --arg k "$k" '.keys[$k].empty_config_today' "$ORACLE")
+        fi
+        [ "$ex" = "$st" ] || { echo "example $k = $ex, standard $st"; return 1; }
+    done < <(yq -r '.profiles.standard | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES")
+    [ "$(yq -r '.loa.profile' "$R/.loa.config.yaml.example")" = "standard" ]
+    # Under the example config the lib resolves standard and no override.
+    LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$R/.loa.config.yaml.example" run bash "$LIB" overrides
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ -z "$output" ]
+}
+
+@test "PL-5 precedence: explicit key beats the profile, the profile beats the fallback" {
+    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\nknown_failures:\n  surface_at_session_start: true\nkarpathy_principles:\n  diff_lines_per_task: 250\n' > "$CFG"
+    [ "$(knob known_failures.surface_at_session_start false)" = "true" ]     # explicit
+    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start true)" = "false" ]          # lean, not the fallback
+    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning true)" = "false" ]   # lean
+    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task 100)" = "250" ]        # non-profile key, explicit
+    [ "$(knob run_mode.stale_hours 7)" = "7" ]                               # non-profile key, fallback
+    printf 'loa:\n  profile: full\n' > "$CFG"
+    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start false)" = "true" ]
+    : > "$CFG"
+    [ "$(bash "$LIB" profile)" = "standard" ]
+    [ "$(bash "$LIB" source)" = "default" ]
+    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning false)" = "true" ]   # standard, not the fallback
+}
+
+@test "PL-6 an explicit false is honoured (yq's // would read it as absent)" {
+    printf 'loa:\n  profile: full\nguardrails:\n  input:\n    enabled: false\n  danger_level:\n    enforce: false\n' > "$CFG"
+    [ "$(knob guardrails.input.enabled true)" = "false" ]
+    [ "$(knob guardrails.danger_level.enforce true)" = "false" ]
+    [ "$(knob .guardrails.input.enabled true)" = "false" ]                   # leading dot accepted
+}
+
+@test "PL-7 an unknown profile warns once on stderr and resolves standard" {

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/profile-floor.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.7 (AC-2.9; PRD
+# AC-9.2; SDD D-9.2, DEC-0166)
+#
+# No profile can reach the floor. The floor source is .claude/data/floor.yaml
+# (read here, never duplicated); its sha256 pin is READ from
+# tests/unit/guard-origins.bats (FLOOR_SHA256) so the two suites cannot
+# disagree. Under `lean` every floor surface reads byte-identically to
+# `standard`: the floor config keys (the two gate skills' flatline_protocol.*
+# config, destructive_command_guard.*, implement_gate.*, hounfour.locality),
+# verdict-derive.sh on fixture feedback files, the adversarial gate's
+# decision and environment, the deny-list file, the fence on the corpus and
+# the FR-1.2b / FR-SZ probes, and user-invoked-commands.txt.
+# =============================================================================
+
+bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
+
+setup() {
+    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
+    LIB="$R/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh"
+    PROFILES="$R/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
+    FLOOR="$R/.claude/data/floor.yaml"
+    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
+    # Two configs that differ ONLY in loa.profile: this repository's own config
+    # (which carries the floor keys it really uses) with the profile set.
+    for p in lean standard; do
+        cp "$R/.loa.config.yaml" "$T/$p.yaml"
+        yq -i ".loa.profile = \"$p\"" "$T/$p.yaml"
+    done
+    unset LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE LOA_PROFILES_FILE
+}
+
+# The floor key patterns, as the lib and the guard register read them.
+floor_keys() { yq -r '.floor_keys[]' "$FLOOR"; }
+
+@test "PF-1 floor.yaml matches the sha256 pin guard-origins.bats carries (one constant, two suites)" {
+    local pin actual
+    pin=$(sed -n 's/^FLOOR_SHA256="\([0-9a-f]\{64\}\)"$/\1/p' "$R/tests/unit/guard-origins.bats")
+    [ -n "$pin" ] || { echo "no FLOOR_SHA256 in guard-origins.bats"; return 1; }
+    actual=$(bash -c 'source "$1/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; sha256_portable "$2"' _ "$R" "$FLOOR" | cut -d' ' -f1)
+    [ "$actual" = "$pin" ] || { echo "floor.yaml sha256 $actual != pinned $pin"; return 1; }
+}
+
+@test "PF-2 no profiles.yaml key matches a floor key or is an ancestor of one" {
+    run python3 -I - "$PROFILES" "$FLOOR" <<'PY'
+import re, subprocess, sys, json
+def load(p):
+    return json.loads(subprocess.check_output(["yq", "-o=json", ".", p]))
+prof, floor = load(sys.argv[1]), load(sys.argv[2])
+keys = sorted({k for v in prof["profiles"].values() for k in v})
+assert len(keys) == 9, keys
+bad = []
+for k in keys:
+    for f in floor["floor_keys"]:
+        rx = "^" + ".+".join(re.escape(s) for s in f.split("*")) + "$"
+        if re.match(rx, k) or f.split("*")[0].startswith(k + "."):
+            bad.append((k, f))
+print("violations:", bad)
+sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
+PY
+    echo "$output"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    # floor_keys_forbidden is not duplicated into profiles.yaml.
+    [ "$(yq -r 'has("floor_keys_forbidden")' "$PROFILES")" = "false" ]
+}
+
+@test "PF-3 under lean the resolved document names no floor key and every floor key reads as under standard" {
+    local p k
+    for p in lean standard; do
+        LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" bash "$LIB" json > "$T/$p.json"
+        [ "$(jq -r '.profile' "$T/$p.json")" = "$p" ]
+    done
+    # Concrete floor keys: every leaf path of this config and the example that a
+    # floor pattern matches (flatline_protocol.*.companion_voice expands here).
+    yq -o=json '.' "$R/.loa.config.yaml" > "$T/cfg.json"
+    yq -o=json '.' "$R/.loa.config.yaml.example" > "$T/ex.json"
+    floor_keys > "$T/floor.txt"
+    python3 -I - "$T/cfg.json" "$T/ex.json" "$T/floor.txt" > "$T/concrete.txt" <<'PY'
+import json, re, sys
+pats = [l.strip() for l in open(sys.argv[3]) if l.strip()]
+rxs = ["^" + ".+".join(re.escape(s) for s in p.split("*")) + "$" for p in pats]
+out = set(p for p in pats if "*" not in p)
+def walk(x, path):
+    if isinstance(x, dict):
+        for k, v in x.items():
+            walk(v, path + [str(k)])
+    if path:
+        key = ".".join(path)
+        if any(re.match(r, key) for r in rxs):
+            out.add(key)
+for f in sys.argv[1:3]:
+    walk(json.load(open(f)), [])
+print("\n".join(sorted(k for k in out if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*", k))))
+PY
+    grep -qx 'flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled' "$T/concrete.txt"
+    grep -qx 'flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled' "$T/concrete.txt"
+    grep -q '^flatline_protocol\.[a-z_]*\.companion_voice$' "$T/concrete.txt"
+    while IFS= read -r k; do
+        [ "$(jq -r --arg k "$k" '.knobs | has($k)' "$T/lean.json")" = "false" ] || { echo "lean resolves floor key $k"; return 1; }
+        a=$(LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/lean.yaml" bash "$LIB" knob "$k" __unset__ 2>/dev/null)
+        b=$(LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/standard.yaml" bash "$LIB" knob "$k" __unset__ 2>/dev/null)
+        [ "$a" = "$b" ] || { echo "$k: lean=$a standard=$b"; return 1; }
+    done < "$T/concrete.txt"
+    # The two gate skills' whole flatline_protocol config is byte-identical.
+    for g in code_review security_audit; do
+        cmp <(yq -o=json ".flatline_protocol.$g" "$T/lean.yaml") <(yq -o=json ".flatline_protocol.$g" "$T/standard.yaml")
+    done
+}

+@test "PF-4 verdict-derive.sh output is byte-identical under lean and standard" {
+    local f p
+    printf 'All good\n\n## Observations\n\n- **LOW** `a.sh:1` — naming\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":0,"low":1},"sprint_id":"sprint-9","ts":"2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' > "$T/ok.md"
+    printf '## Changes Required\n\n- **HIGH** `a.sh:1` — unchecked input\n\nAll good\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED","counts":{"critical":0,"high":1,"medium":0,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-9","ts":"2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' > "$T/bad.md"
+    for f in ok bad; do
+        for p in lean standard; do
+            rc=0
+            LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" bash "$R/.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh" --file "$T/$f.md" --gate review --json \
+                > "$T/vd-$f-$p.out" 2>&1 || rc=$?
+            echo "$rc" >> "$T/vd-$f-$p.out"
+        done
+        cmp "$T/vd-$f-lean.out" "$T/vd-$f-standard.out"
+    done
+    # The fixtures exercise both outcomes, so identity is not vacuous.
+    ! cmp -s "$T/vd-ok-lean.out" "$T/vd-bad-lean.out"
+}

+@test "PF-5 the adversarial-review gate decides identically under lean and standard" {
+    local d="$T/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-999" p rc
+    mkdir -p "$d"
+    for p in lean standard; do
+        yq -i '.flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled = true' "$T/$p.yaml"
+        rc=0
+        printf '{"tool_name":"Write","tool_input":{"file_path":"%s/COMPLETED"}}' "$d" \
+            | env -u LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" LOA_CONFIG_PATH_OVERRIDE="$T/$p.yaml" \
+              bash "$R/.claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh" > "$T/gate-$p.out" 2>&1 || rc=$?
+        echo "$rc" >> "$T/gate-$p.out"
+    done
+    cmp "$T/gate-lean.out" "$T/gate-standard.out"
+    # No dissent envelope for an enabled gate: the gate refuses (exit 2) under both.
+    [ "$(tail -1 "$T/gate-lean.out")" = "2" ]
+    # The gate's environment knob is not a profile key and the gate never sources the lib.
+    ! grep -q 'profile-lib' "$R/.claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh"
+    ! yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | grep -qi 'adversarial'
+}
+
+@test "PF-6 the fence decides every corpus row and the FR-1.2b / FR-SZ probes identically under lean and standard" {
+    local p row cmd rc id
+    jq -r '.id' "$R/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl" > /dev/null
+    # Floor probes (the corpus carries the floor rules named in floor.yaml floor_corpus when they exist).
+    printf '%s\n' \
+        '{"id":"FP-1","cmd":"git stash pop 2>/dev/null"}' \
+        '{"id":"FP-2","cmd":"git stash push -m x | tail -1"}' \
+        '{"id":"FP-3","cmd":"echo x > .claude/hooks/evil.sh"}' \
+        '{"id":"FP-4","cmd":"cp /tmp/a .claude/settings.json"}' \
+        '{"id":"FP-5","cmd":"sed -i s/a/b/ .claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh"}' > "$T/probes.jsonl"
+    cat "$R/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl" "$T/probes.jsonl" > "$T/all.jsonl"
+    for p in lean standard; do
+        mkdir -p "$T/root-$p/repo"
+        cp "$T/$p.yaml" "$T/root-$p/.loa.config.yaml"
+        : > "$T/fence-$p.txt"
+        while IFS= read -r row; do
+            [ -n "$row" ] || continue
+            id=$(jq -r '.id' <<<"$row"); cmd=$(jq -r '.cmd' <<<"$row")
+            rc=0
+            (cd "$T/root-$p/repo" && jq -cn --arg c "$cmd" '{tool_input: {command: $c}}' \

+                  bash "$R/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1) || rc=$?
+            echo "$id $rc" >> "$T/fence-$p.txt"
+        done < "$T/all.jsonl"
+    done
+    cmp "$T/fence-lean.txt" "$T/fence-standard.txt"
+    for id in FP-1 FP-2 FP-3 FP-4 FP-5; do
+        grep -qx "$id 2" "$T/fence-lean.txt" || { echo "$id not blocked under lean: $(grep "^$id " "$T/fence-lean.txt")"; return 1; }

+    while IFS= read -r rule; do

+            "$R/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl" | while IFS= read -r id; do
+            grep -q "^$id " "$T/fence-lean.txt"
+        done
+    done < <(yq -r '.floor_corpus.rules[]' "$FLOOR")
+}

+@test "PF-7 the deny list, the System-Zone rules and user-invoked-commands.txt are untouched by resolving any profile" {
+    local f before after p
+    for f in .claude/hooks/settings.deny.json .claude/data/user-invoked-commands.txt .claude/rules/zone-system.md .claude/data/floor.yaml; do
+        before=$(bash -c 'source "$1/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; sha256_portable "$1/$2"' _ "$R" "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)
+        for p in lean standard; do
+            LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE="$T/cache-$p.json" bash "$LIB" json >/dev/null
+        done
+        after=$(bash -c 'source "$1/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; sha256_portable "$1/$2"' _ "$R" "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)
+        [ "$before" = "$after" ]

+    ! grep -Eq 'settings\.deny|user-invoked-commands|zone-system' "$LIB"

+    [ "$(jq -r '.profile' "$T/cache-lean.json")" = "lean" ]
+    [ "$(jq -c '.profile_keys' "$T/cache-lean.json")" = "$(jq -c '.profile_keys' "$T/cache-standard.json")" ]
+}

+@test "PL-1 every profile defines every key, and the key set is the nine optional keys" {

+        [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    done
+    [ "$(yq -r '.profiles | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort | paste -sd, -)" = "full,lean,standard" ]
+    [ "$(yq -r '.schema_version' "$PROFILES")" = "1" ]
+    ! yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | grep -qx 'interview.pacing'

+
+@test "PL-2 every profile value is a boolean; lean is all false and full all true" {

+    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles.lean[]] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "false" ]
+    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles.full[]] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "true" ]

+@test "PL-3 standard equals the oracle captured before any reader changed" {

+    done < <(jq -r '.keys | keys[]' "$ORACLE")

+    run jq -r '.keys | to_entries[] | select(.key | startswith("guardrails.") | not)

+@test "PL-4 standard equals the post-cycle example defaults (explicit example value, else the reader's fallback)" {
