+# ledger STATUS101 STATUS102 STATUS103 [EXTRA-SPRINT-JSON]
+ledger() {
+  jq -n --arg a "$1" --arg b "$2" --arg c "$3" --argjson x "${4:-null}" '
+    {schema_version: 1, active_cycle: "cycle-x", next_sprint_number: 104,
+     cycles: [
+       {id: "cycle-old", status: "archived", created: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
+        sprints: [{global_id: 1, local_label: "sprint-1", status: "completed", created: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"}]},
+       {id: "cycle-x", status: "active", created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
+        sprints: ([{global_id: 101, local_label: "sprint-1", status: $a, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
+                   {global_id: 102, local_label: "sprint-2", status: $b, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
+                   {global_id: 103, local_label: "sprint-3", status: $c, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}]
+                  + (if $x == null then [] else [$x] end))}]}' > "$R/grimoires/loa/ledger.json"
+}
+
+# feedback GID GATE VERDICT [SPRINT_ID] [ROUND] [MEDIUM] [TS] — a feedback file whose trailer verdict-derive accepts
+feedback() {
+  local gid="$1" gate="$2" verdict="$3" sid="${4:-sprint-$1}" round="${5:-}" med="${6:-0}" ts="${7:-2026-06-01T00:00:00Z}" f prose
+  mkdir -p "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$gid"
+  if [[ "$gate" == review ]]; then f=engineer-feedback; else f=auditor-sprint-feedback; fi
+  [[ -n "$round" ]] && f="$f-r$round"
+  if [[ "$verdict" == APPROVED ]]; then
+    if [[ "$gate" == review ]]; then prose='All good'; else prose="APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO"; fi
+  else
+    prose=$'# Feedback\n\n## Findings\n\n- MEDIUM: something to fix'
+  fi
+  printf '%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":%s,"low":0},"sprint_id":"%s","ts":"%s"} -->\n' \
+    "$prose" "$gate" "$verdict" "$med" "$sid" "$ts" > "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$gid/$f.md"
+}
+
+# complete GID [SPRINT_ID] — review + audit APPROVED and the COMPLETED marker
+complete() {
+  feedback "$1" review APPROVED "${2:-}"
+  feedback "$1" audit APPROVED "${2:-}"
+  printf 'COMPLETED 2026-06-01T00:00:00Z\nsprint: %s\n' "${2:-sprint-$1}" > "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$1/COMPLETED"
+}
+
+# cache STATE [AGE_HOURS] [EXTRA-JQ] — .run/sprint-plan-state.json (jq now: portable, no GNU date -d)
+cache() {
+  jq -n --arg s "$1" --argjson h "${2:-0}" '
+    {schema_version: 2, plan_id: "plan-x", branch: "feature/x", state: $s,
+     timestamps: {started: "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z", last_activity: (now - $h * 3600 | floor | todate)},
+     sprints: {total: 3, completed: 0, current: "sprint-1",
+               list: [{id: "sprint-1", status: "in_progress"}, {id: "sprint-2", status: "pending"}, {id: "sprint-3", status: "pending"}]}}
+    '"${3:+| $3}" > "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"
+}

+derive() { run --separate-stderr bash "$CK" derive --root "$R" "$@"; }
+_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }
+dj() { jq -r "$1" <<<"$output"; }

+# (PRD FR-5 AC-5.1 … AC-5.4, FR-4(f) AC-4.6; SDD D-5.1, D-5.1a, D-5.2, D-5.3, D-5.4)
+# `run-checkpoint.sh derive` rebuilds the run position from files: one case per
+# decision-table row, the breaker recompute from the feedback history, the
+# write path and its rollback knob, and one case per known reader over a
+# derived file. Fixture: a tiny git repo with a ledger, a2a/ and .run/ in a
+# temp dir; nothing touches this checkout's .run/.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
+  CK="$REPO/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh"
+  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rcd.XXXXXX")"

+teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }

+# ledger STATUS101 STATUS102 STATUS103 [EXTRA-SPRINT-JSON]
+ledger() {
+  jq -n --arg a "$1" --arg b "$2" --arg c "$3" --argjson x "${4:-null}" '
+    {schema_version: 1, active_cycle: "cycle-x", next_sprint_number: 104,
+     cycles: [
+       {id: "cycle-old", status: "archived", created: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
+        sprints: [{global_id: 1, local_label: "sprint-1", status: "completed", created: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"}]},
+       {id: "cycle-x", status: "active", created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
+        sprints: ([{global_id: 101, local_label: "sprint-1", status: $a, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
+                   {global_id: 102, local_label: "sprint-2", status: $b, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
+                   {global_id: 103, local_label: "sprint-3", status: $c, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}]
+                  + (if $x == null then [] else [$x] end))}]}' > "$R/grimoires/loa/ledger.json"
+}

+# feedback GID GATE VERDICT [SPRINT_ID] [ROUND] [MEDIUM] [TS] — a feedback file whose trailer verdict-derive accepts
+feedback() {
+  local gid="$1" gate="$2" verdict="$3" sid="${4:-sprint-$1}" round="${5:-}" med="${6:-0}" ts="${7:-2026-06-01T00:00:00Z}" f prose
+  mkdir -p "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$gid"
+  if [[ "$gate" == review ]]; then f=engineer-feedback; else f=auditor-sprint-feedback; fi
+  [[ -n "$round" ]] && f="$f-r$round"
+  if [[ "$verdict" == APPROVED ]]; then
+    if [[ "$gate" == review ]]; then prose='All good'; else prose="APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO"; fi
+  else
+    prose=$'# Feedback\n\n## Findings\n\n- MEDIUM: something to fix'
+  fi
+  printf '%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":%s,"low":0},"sprint_id":"%s","ts":"%s"} -->\n' \
+    "$prose" "$gate" "$verdict" "$med" "$sid" "$ts" > "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$gid/$f.md"

+# complete GID [SPRINT_ID] — review + audit APPROVED and the COMPLETED marker
+complete() {
+  feedback "$1" review APPROVED "${2:-}"
+  feedback "$1" audit APPROVED "${2:-}"

+derive() { run --separate-stderr bash "$CK" derive --root "$R" "$@"; }
+_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }

@@ -0,0 +1,154 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/run-checkpoint-record-round.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 2 Task 2.5
+# (PRD FR-4(f) AC-4.6; SDD D-4.6). `run-checkpoint.sh record-round` replaces the
+# run-mode SKILL's breaker prose: the same-issue hash from the derived verdict,
+# no-progress, cycle count, timeout; a trip writes OPEN + HALTED and exits 10.
+# All files live in a temp dir.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
+  CK="$REPO/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh"
+  VD="$REPO/.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh"
+  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rcr.XXXXXX")"
+  mkdir -p "$T/.run" "$T/a2a"
+  B="$T/.run/circuit-breaker.json"
+  S="$T/.run/state.json"
+  printf '{"run_id":"r","state":"RUNNING","phase":"REVIEW"}\n' > "$S"
+}
+teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
+
+# fb NAME GATE VERDICT [MEDIUM] — a feedback file verdict-derive accepts
+fb() {
+  local prose
+  if [[ "$3" == APPROVED ]]; then
+    if [[ "$2" == review ]]; then prose='All good'; else prose="APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO"; fi
+  else
+    prose=$'# Feedback\n\n## Findings\n\n- MEDIUM: fix it'
+  fi
+  printf '%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":%s,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-1","ts":"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' \
+    "$prose" "$2" "$3" "${4:-0}" > "$T/a2a/$1"
+}
+
+_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }
+
+breaker() {  # $1 jq tweak over a CLOSED breaker started now
+  jq -n '{state: "CLOSED",
+          triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: 3, last_hash: null}, no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: 5},
+                     cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: 20}, timeout: {started: (now | floor | todate), limit_hours: 8}},
+          history: []}'"${1:+ | $1}" > "$B"
+}
+
+rr() { run --separate-stderr bash "$CK" record-round --root "$T" --breaker "$B" --state-file "$S" --sprint sprint-1 "$@"; }
+
+@test "RCR-1 a CHANGES_REQUIRED review increments cycle_count.current, sets same_issue {count 1, last_hash} to the SKILL's derived hash, exit 0" {
+  breaker
+  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [[ "$output" == "recorded: review CHANGES_REQUIRED — cycle 1/20, same_issue 1/3, no_progress 0/5" ]]
+  local want
+  want=$(bash "$VD" --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md" --gate review --json 2>/dev/null | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
+  run jq -r '[.state, .triggers.cycle_count.current, .triggers.same_issue.count, .triggers.same_issue.last_hash, (.history | length)] | map(tostring) | join(" ")' "$B"
+  [ "$output" = "CLOSED 1 1 $want 0" ]
+  [ "$(jq -r .state "$S")" = RUNNING ]
+}
+
+@test "RCR-2 the same hash again counts up; a different finding set resets same_issue to 1 with the new last_hash" {
+  breaker
+  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.count "$B")" = 2 ]
+  local h1; h1=$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.last_hash "$B")
+  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 2
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.count "$B")" = 1 ]
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.last_hash "$B")" != "$h1" ]
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.cycle_count.current "$B")" = 3 ]
+}
+
+@test "RCR-3 no_progress counts consecutive rounds whose counts are unchanged and resets when they change" {
+  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99'
+  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.no_progress.count "$B")" = 0 ]
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.no_progress.count "$B")" = 2 ]
+  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 3
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.no_progress.count "$B")" = 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "RCR-4 a trip at threshold writes state OPEN, appends one history entry, sets .run/state.json HALTED, prints TRIPPED and exits 10" {
+  breaker
+  fb auditor-sprint-feedback.md audit CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
+  rr --gate audit --file "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
+  rr --gate audit --file "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  rr --gate audit --file "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
+  [[ "$output" == *$'\n'"TRIPPED: same_issue: same issue hash "*" seen 3 times in a row" ]]
+  run jq -r '[.state, (.history | length), .history[0].trigger, .history[0].gate, .history[0].sprint] | map(tostring) | join(" ")' "$B"
+  [ "$output" = "OPEN 1 same_issue audit sprint-1" ]
+  [ "$(jq -r '.state + " " + .run_id' "$S")" = "HALTED r" ]
+  # a further round on an OPEN breaker still exits 10 and does not duplicate the history entry
+  rr --gate audit --file "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
+  [ "$(jq -r '.history | length' "$B")" = 1 ]
+}
+
+@test "RCR-5 the cycle limit, the no-progress threshold and the timeout trip in that documented order" {
+  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
+  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99 | .triggers.cycle_count.current = 19'
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
+  [[ "$output" == *"TRIPPED: cycle_count: 20 changes-required rounds reached the limit 20" ]]
+  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99 | .triggers.no_progress.count = 4 | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = "{\"critical\":0,\"high\":0,\"medium\":1,\"low\":0}"'
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
+  [[ "$output" == *"TRIPPED: no_progress: "* ]]
+  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99 | .triggers.timeout.started = (now - 9 * 3600 | floor | todate)'
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
+  [[ "$output" == *"TRIPPED: timeout: run older than 8 hours" ]]
+  [ "$(jq -r .history[-1].trigger "$B")" = timeout ]
+}
+
+@test "RCR-6 APPROVED leaves every counter and the run state as they were (exit 0)" {
+  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.count = 2 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = "abc" | .triggers.cycle_count.current = 4 | .triggers.no_progress.count = 1'
+  cp "$B" "$T/before"
+  fb engineer-feedback.md review APPROVED
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [[ "$output" == "recorded: review APPROVED — breaker counters unchanged" ]]
+  cmp "$T/before" "$B"
+  [ "$(jq -r .state "$S")" = RUNNING ]
+}
+
+@test "RCR-7 an inconsistent APPROVED trailer counts as findings; a legacy file without a trailer hashes its findings section; a missing breaker file is created from the schema defaults" {
+  printf 'Looks fine\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":0,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-1","ts":"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' > "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
+  rr --gate audit --file "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  run jq -r '[.state, .triggers.cycle_count.current, .triggers.cycle_count.limit, .triggers.same_issue.threshold, .triggers.no_progress.threshold, .triggers.timeout.limit_hours] | map(tostring) | join(" ")' "$B"
+  [ "$output" = "CLOSED 1 20 3 5 8" ]
+  printf '# Review\n\n## Findings\n\n- a legacy finding\n' > "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  local want
+  want=$(grep -A 100 "## Findings\|## Issues\|## Changes Required" "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md" | head -50 | _md5)
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.last_hash "$B")" = "$want" ]
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.cycle_count.current "$B")" = 2 ]
+}
+

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
+# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
+#
+# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
+# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
+# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
+# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
+# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
+# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
+# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
+# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
+#
+# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
+# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
+#
+# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
+# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+ROOT="."
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
+[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
+command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
+[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }
+# Alternation of the dot-escaped keys; each must be preceded by a dot that is
+# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
+alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)
+pattern="(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)"
+
+hits=$(cd "$ROOT" && grep -rnE "$pattern" .claude tools 2>/dev/null \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?\.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib\.sh:' \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?tools/check-knob-readers\.sh:' || true)
+if [[ -n "$hits" ]]; then
+  echo "check-knob-readers.sh: direct read(s) of a profile key; use loa_knob from .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:" >&2
+  printf '%s\n' "$hits" | cut -c1-240 >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no direct profile-key reads ($(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') keys checked)"

@@ -0,0 +1,154 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/run-checkpoint-record-round.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 2 Task 2.5
+# (PRD FR-4(f) AC-4.6; SDD D-4.6). `run-checkpoint.sh record-round` replaces the
+# run-mode SKILL's breaker prose: the same-issue hash from the derived verdict,
+# no-progress, cycle count, timeout; a trip writes OPEN + HALTED and exits 10.
+# All files live in a temp dir.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
+  CK="$REPO/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh"
+  VD="$REPO/.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh"
+  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rcr.XXXXXX")"
+  mkdir -p "$T/.run" "$T/a2a"
+  B="$T/.run/circuit-breaker.json"
+  S="$T/.run/state.json"
+  printf '{"run_id":"r","state":"RUNNING","phase":"REVIEW"}\n' > "$S"
+}
+teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
+
+# fb NAME GATE VERDICT [MEDIUM] — a feedback file verdict-derive accepts
+fb() {
+  local prose
+  if [[ "$3" == APPROVED ]]; then
+    if [[ "$2" == review ]]; then prose='All good'; else prose="APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO"; fi
+  else
+    prose=$'# Feedback\n\n## Findings\n\n- MEDIUM: fix it'
+  fi
+  printf '%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":%s,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-1","ts":"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' \
+    "$prose" "$2" "$3" "${4:-0}" > "$T/a2a/$1"
+}
+
+_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }
+
+breaker() {  # $1 jq tweak over a CLOSED breaker started now
+  jq -n '{state: "CLOSED",
+          triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: 3, last_hash: null}, no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: 5},
+                     cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: 20}, timeout: {started: (now | floor | todate), limit_hours: 8}},
+          history: []}'"${1:+ | $1}" > "$B"
+}
+
+rr() { run --separate-stderr bash "$CK" record-round --root "$T" --breaker "$B" --state-file "$S" --sprint sprint-1 "$@"; }
+
+@test "RCR-1 a CHANGES_REQUIRED review increments cycle_count.current, sets same_issue {count 1, last_hash} to the SKILL's derived hash, exit 0" {
+  breaker
+  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [[ "$output" == "recorded: review CHANGES_REQUIRED — cycle 1/20, same_issue 1/3, no_progress 0/5" ]]
+  local want
+  want=$(bash "$VD" --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md" --gate review --json 2>/dev/null | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
+  run jq -r '[.state, .triggers.cycle_count.current, .triggers.same_issue.count, .triggers.same_issue.last_hash, (.history | length)] | map(tostring) | join(" ")' "$B"
+  [ "$output" = "CLOSED 1 1 $want 0" ]
+  [ "$(jq -r .state "$S")" = RUNNING ]
+}
+
+@test "RCR-2 the same hash again counts up; a different finding set resets same_issue to 1 with the new last_hash" {
+  breaker
+  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.count "$B")" = 2 ]
+  local h1; h1=$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.last_hash "$B")
+  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 2
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.count "$B")" = 1 ]
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.last_hash "$B")" != "$h1" ]
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.cycle_count.current "$B")" = 3 ]
+}
+
+@test "RCR-3 no_progress counts consecutive rounds whose counts are unchanged and resets when they change" {
+  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99'
+  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.no_progress.count "$B")" = 0 ]
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.no_progress.count "$B")" = 2 ]
+  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 3
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.no_progress.count "$B")" = 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "RCR-4 a trip at threshold writes state OPEN, appends one history entry, sets .run/state.json HALTED, prints TRIPPED and exits 10" {
+  breaker
+  fb auditor-sprint-feedback.md audit CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
+  rr --gate audit --file "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
+  rr --gate audit --file "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  rr --gate audit --file "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
+  [[ "$output" == *$'\n'"TRIPPED: same_issue: same issue hash "*" seen 3 times in a row" ]]
+  run jq -r '[.state, (.history | length), .history[0].trigger, .history[0].gate, .history[0].sprint] | map(tostring) | join(" ")' "$B"
+  [ "$output" = "OPEN 1 same_issue audit sprint-1" ]
+  [ "$(jq -r '.state + " " + .run_id' "$S")" = "HALTED r" ]
+  # a further round on an OPEN breaker still exits 10 and does not duplicate the history entry
+  rr --gate audit --file "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
+  [ "$(jq -r '.history | length' "$B")" = 1 ]
+}
+
+@test "RCR-5 the cycle limit, the no-progress threshold and the timeout trip in that documented order" {
+  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
+  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99 | .triggers.cycle_count.current = 19'
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
+  [[ "$output" == *"TRIPPED: cycle_count: 20 changes-required rounds reached the limit 20" ]]
+  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99 | .triggers.no_progress.count = 4 | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = "{\"critical\":0,\"high\":0,\"medium\":1,\"low\":0}"'
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
+  [[ "$output" == *"TRIPPED: no_progress: "* ]]
+  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99 | .triggers.timeout.started = (now - 9 * 3600 | floor | todate)'
+  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
+  [[ "$output" == *"TRIPPED: timeout: run older than 8 hours" ]]
+  [ "$(jq -r .history[-1].trigger "$B")" = timeout ]
+}
+
+@test "RCR-6 APPROVED leaves every counter and the run state as they were (exit 0)" {
+  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.count = 2 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = "abc" | .triggers.cycle_count.current = 4 | .triggers.no_progress.count = 1'

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
+# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
+#
+# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
+# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
+# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
+# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
+# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
+# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
+# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
+# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
+#
+# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
+# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
+#
+# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
+# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+ROOT="."
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
+[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
+command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
+[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }
+# Alternation of the dot-escaped keys; each must be preceded by a dot that is
+# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
+alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)
+pattern="(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)"
+

+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?\.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib\.sh:' \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?tools/check-knob-readers\.sh:' || true)

# =============================================================================

# Read tool input from stdin (not for --effective-mode, which reads no payload)
input=""
if [[ "${1:-}" != "--effective-mode" ]]; then
    input=$(cat 2>/dev/null) || input=""
fi

# The ask reply; jq builds it so any reason is a well-formed JSON string (run-3 finding 7); the printf literal is only
# for the jq-missing branch, whose reason is a fixed string
emit_ask() {
    if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
        jq -nc --arg r "$1" '{hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"ask",permissionDecisionReason:$r}}'
    else
        printf '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"%s"}}\n' "$1"
    fi
}

# Byte sequences strip_controls removes: UTF-8 C1 controls (C2 80..C2 9F) and the format/bidi code points
# U+200B-U+200F, U+2028-U+202E, U+2060-U+2064, U+2066-U+206F, U+FEFF, U+00AD, U+061C, U+180E, U+FE00-U+FE0F,
# U+FFF9-U+FFFB and the tag characters U+E0001, U+E0020-U+E007F (run-3 finding 5); each sequence starts with a lead
# byte, so a byte-wise match never lands inside another character
# printf -v keeps this portable (no GNU-sed \x); built on first use, not on every Write/Edit (BB-008)
_IG_STRIP_SEQS=()
_ig_strip_seqs_init() {
    local _ig_i _ig_hex _ig_seq
    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 160; _ig_i++ )); do
        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xc2\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    done
    for _ig_hex in 8b 8c 8d 8e 8f a8 a9 aa ab ac ad ae; do
        printf -v _ig_seq "\\xe2\\x80\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    done
    for _ig_hex in a0 a1 a2 a3 a4 a6 a7 a8 a9 aa ab ac ad ae af; do
        printf -v _ig_seq "\\xe2\\x81\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    done
    for _ig_seq in '\xef\xbb\xbf' '\xc2\xad' '\xd8\x9c' '\xe1\xa0\x8e' '\xef\xbf\xb9' '\xef\xbf\xba' '\xef\xbf\xbb' '\xf3\xa0\x80\x81'; do
        printf -v _ig_seq "$_ig_seq"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    done
    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 144; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+FE00-U+FE0F = EF B8 80..EF B8 8F
        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xef\\xb8\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    done
    for (( _ig_i = 160; _ig_i < 192; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+E0020-U+E003F = F3 A0 80 A0..F3 A0 80 BF
        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xf3\\xa0\\x80\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    done
    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 192; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+E0040-U+E007F = F3 A0 81 80..F3 A0 81 BF
        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xf3\\xa0\\x81\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")

# Sets the variable named $1 to at most 256 bytes of $2, never ending inside a UTF-8 character: a trailing lead byte
# whose sequence the cut left short, or stray continuation bytes, are dropped (run-3 finding 5; jq would read a split
# character as U+FFFD). printf -v, not $(...), so a trailing newline in a raw value survives into the audit row
cut_utf8_256() {
    local LC_ALL=C
    local _c_s=${2:0:256} _c_n _c_i _c_b _c_need
    _c_n=${#_c_s}
    for (( _c_i = _c_n - 1; _c_i >= 0 && _c_i >= _c_n - 4; _c_i-- )); do
        printf -v _c_b '%d' "'${_c_s:_c_i:1}"
        (( _c_b >= 128 && _c_b < 192 )) && continue   # continuation byte: keep walking back to its lead
        if (( _c_b < 128 )); then _c_need=1; elif (( _c_b < 224 )); then _c_need=2; elif (( _c_b < 240 )); then _c_need=3; else _c_need=4; fi
        if (( _c_n - _c_i < _c_need )); then _c_s=${_c_s:0:_c_i}          # the cut left this character short
        elif (( _c_n - _c_i > _c_need )); then _c_s=${_c_s:0:_c_i+_c_need}   # continuation bytes after a complete character are stray
        fi

        return 0
    done
    printf -v "$1" '%s' "${_c_s:0:_c_i+1}"   # only continuation bytes at the end: drop them

# passes over a short string), then C0 and DEL, then the sequences above byte-wise until nothing changes (deleting
# one sequence can join its neighbours into another: C2 C2 9B 9B)
strip_controls() {
    local LC_ALL=C s prev seq

    while :; do
        prev=$s
        for seq in "${_IG_STRIP_SEQS[@]}"; do s=${s//"$seq"/}; done
        [[ "$s" == "$prev" ]] && break
    done
    printf '%s' "$s"

+## Rules and arming
+
+These five rules govern every team. Until cycle-129 they were the C-TEAM rows of `constraints.json`, rendered into the always-loaded kernel on every turn; they now live here only (DEC-0140), because no harness surface runs on teammate spawn and the rows cost every single-agent session their bytes. The ids stay as names.
+
+| Id | Rule | Why |
+|----|------|-----|
+| C-TEAM-001 | Planning, orchestration, deployment and lifecycle skills are lead-only; teammates implement, review and audit only (the Skill Invocation Matrix below is the full list) | Planning skills produce single artifacts (PRD, SDD, sprint plan) that assume single-writer semantics; concurrent invocation would corrupt state |
+| C-TEAM-002 | All beads (`br`) operations go through the lead; teammates report via SendMessage | Beads uses SQLite with single-writer semantics; concurrent br sync or br close causes lock contention and potential corruption |
+| C-TEAM-003 | Only the lead writes `.run/` state files (`simstim-state.json`, `bridge-state.json`, `sprint-plan-state.json`); teammates report status via SendMessage | State files use read-modify-write pattern; concurrent writes cause lost updates and inconsistent reads |
+| C-TEAM-004 | Git commit and push go through the lead; teammates report completed work via SendMessage | Git's working tree and index are shared mutable state; concurrent commits or pushes cause merge conflicts, index lock failures, and corrupted state |
+| C-TEAM-005 | Teammates never modify the System Zone (`.claude/`): framework configuration, constraint definitions, hook scripts and schema files are lead-only | System Zone modifications by a teammate could alter constraint definitions, hook behavior, or skill configurations for all agents in the team, breaking the coordination invariants that other C-TEAM constraints depend on |
+
+**Arming.** The three team hooks (`team-role-guard.sh`, `team-role-guard-write.sh`, `team-skill-guard.sh`) stay registered but are no-ops until the lead exports `LOA_TEAM_MEMBER` (the teammate's name) into each teammate's environment before spawning it. Without that variable the rules above are prose the teammate is asked to follow, and the review and audit gates are the safety net. The guard register lists the three hooks as `dormant` with `LOA_TEAM_MEMBER` as their knob (`.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml`).
+

 **Defense-in-depth posture (cycle-111)**: this hook is a fence against routine destructive mistakes by autonomous agents — NOT a hardened security boundary. Documented accepted bypass classes (cycle-111 SDD §11): newline statement separators, subshell wrapping (`bash -c '...'` quoted-differently, `$(...)`), eval/base64 decode, SQL comments containing WHERE, python scripts loaded from disk, jq absent from PATH. ERE flavor: GNU/BSD-compatible extensions (`\s`, `\b`), NOT strict POSIX. Latency budget: p95 < 80ms across 100 invocations (bash startup + jq + 13 grep passes).
 
+### Heredoc consumer classification (cycle-129 FR-6)
+
+Knob: `destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier` (default `true`; `false` restores the pre-cycle scan and is the rollback key). The fence reads the knob from `.loa.config.yaml` only for commands that hold `<<`. The full grammar, both class lists and the default are stated in the block comment above `_bdb_hd_is_interp` in `block-destructive-bash.sh`. In summary:
+
+- **Grammar.** The fence sees literal command text, with CRLF folded to LF. A control character, an unreadable header, more than one heredoc on a header, a non-word or variable delimiter, or a missing terminator makes the whole command scan in full.
+- **Interpreter class.** The body is scanned exactly as before. This applies when the consumer or any pipe target is a shell, interpreter, argument-running wrapper or SQL runner, when the statement holds a substitution, group or continuation, or when an allowlisted form carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag. It also applies when the write target is executable content: a script extension, a shebang first line, `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/settings*.json`, `.git/hooks/`, an rc or profile file, `/etc`, or a directory on `PATH`. Naming the target elsewhere on the same command outside a safe reader has the same effect.
+- **Non-executing class.** This covers exact forms only: `cat`, `tee`, `printf` and `echo` to a plain file or stdout, `gh pr|issue comment -F -`, `gh pr create --body-file -`, `git commit -F -`, `br create|update` reading stdin, `jq`/`yq` without in-place, `grep`, print-only `sed -n`, `sort` and `wc`. Their bodies are scanned per segment. Segments that start with a fence verb are kept for the normal rules, and the rest are dropped. A substitution under an unquoted delimiter, an interpreter word or a variable command word sends the body back to a full scan.
+- **Default.** A consumer on neither list, or a parse failure, scans in full. The #1245 quoted standalone `cat` scrub is the special case and is also the knob-off path.
+- **Export.** Source the hook with `BDB_LIB_ONLY=1` and call `_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command>`, which prints `interpreter`, `nonexec` or `none`. `heredoc_nonexec <command>` exits 0 for a non-executing heredoc. Library mode applies only when the file is sourced. An executed hook ignores the variable.
+- **Remaining gap.** A body written to a plain file by one command and executed by a later command is outside a per-command fence. The Write tool shares this limit.
+
 **Accepted false positives (quote-blindness residue, cycle-120 C-D3)**: the inert-carrier scrub redacts a known data carrier's value (git commit `-m`, `br`/`bd -d`, `gh … create --body/--title`, `echo`/`printf`) only when the value holds **neither `$(` nor a backtick**. A lone `$` (dollar amount, `$ENV` mention, trailing bare `$`) is now permitted inside a redacted value — so `git commit -m "saved $5 by dropping find . -exec rm -rf {} +"` correctly ALLOWs. One residual false positive is **accepted by design**:
 
 - **Case A — a `$(…)` command-substitution inside a carrier value** (e.g. a multi-line commit body wrapped in `$(cat <<'EOF' … find -exec rm -rf … EOF)`). The `$(` disqualifies the value from redaction (a regex fence cannot parse subshell contents without reintroducing the #1047 bypass), so a destructive *shape* mentioned inside that subshell body still trips FR-2 and blocks a genuinely safe commit. **Workaround**: paraphrase the destructive shape in the commit body (as the cycle-119 commits did — e.g. write "find-exec-rm" rather than the literal `find … -exec rm -rf`), or drop the `$(…)` wrapper. This is a preserved false positive, never a bypass: leaving `$(`/backtick values un-redacted is what keeps command-substitution smuggling (`git commit -m "$(rm -rf /)"`) caught. Backtick command-substitution itself remains the separately-tracked, uncaught pre-existing gap (bd-bdb-backtick-bypass).

+### Heredoc consumer classification (cycle-129 FR-6)
+
+Knob: `destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier` (default `true`; `false` restores the pre-cycle scan and is the rollback key). The fence reads the knob from `.loa.config.yaml` only for commands that hold `<<`. The full grammar, both class lists and the default are stated in the block comment above `_bdb_hd_is_interp` in `block-destructive-bash.sh`. In summary:
+
+- **Grammar.** The fence sees literal command text, with CRLF folded to LF. A control character, an unreadable header, more than one heredoc on a header, a non-word or variable delimiter, or a missing terminator makes the whole command scan in full.
+- **Interpreter class.** The body is scanned exactly as before. This applies when the consumer or any pipe target is a shell, interpreter, argument-running wrapper or SQL runner, when the statement holds a substitution, group or continuation, or when an allowlisted form carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag. It also applies when the write target is executable content: a script extension, a shebang first line, `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/settings*.json`, `.git/hooks/`, an rc or profile file, `/etc`, or a directory on `PATH`. Naming the target elsewhere on the same command outside a safe reader has the same effect.
+- **Non-executing class.** This covers exact forms only: `cat`, `tee`, `printf` and `echo` to a plain file or stdout, `gh pr|issue comment -F -`, `gh pr create --body-file -`, `git commit -F -`, `br create|update` reading stdin, `jq`/`yq` without in-place, `grep`, print-only `sed -n`, `sort` and `wc`. Their bodies are scanned per segment. Segments that start with a fence verb are kept for the normal rules, and the rest are dropped. A substitution under an unquoted delimiter, an interpreter word or a variable command word sends the body back to a full scan.
+- **Default.** A consumer on neither list, or a parse failure, scans in full. The #1245 quoted standalone `cat` scrub is the special case and is also the knob-off path.
+- **Export.** Source the hook with `BDB_LIB_ONLY=1` and call `_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command>`, which prints `interpreter`, `nonexec` or `none`. `heredoc_nonexec <command>` exits 0 for a non-executing heredoc. Library mode applies only when the file is sourced. An executed hook ignores the variable.
+- **Remaining gap.** A body written to a plain file by one command and executed by a later command is outside a per-command fence. The Write tool shares this limit.
+
 **Accepted false positives (quote-blindness residue, cycle-120 C-D3)**: the inert-carrier scrub redacts a known data carrier's value (git commit `-m`, `br`/`bd -d`, `gh … create --body/--title`, `echo`/`printf`) only when the value holds **neither `$(` nor a backtick**. A lone `$` (dollar amount, `$ENV` mention, trailing bare `$`) is now permitted inside a redacted value — so `git commit -m "saved $5 by dropping find . -exec rm -rf {} +"` correctly ALLOWs. One residual false positive is **accepted by design**:
 
 - **Case A — a `$(…)` command-substitution inside a carrier value** (e.g. a multi-line commit body wrapped in `$(cat <<'EOF' … find -exec rm -rf … EOF)`). The `$(` disqualifies the value from redaction (a regex fence cannot parse subshell contents without reintroducing the #1047 bypass), so a destructive *shape* mentioned inside that subshell body still trips FR-2 and blocks a genuinely safe commit. **Workaround**: paraphrase the destructive shape in the commit body (as the cycle-119 commits did — e.g. write "find-exec-rm" rather than the literal `find … -exec rm -rf`), or drop the `$(…)` wrapper. This is a preserved false positive, never a bypass: leaving `$(`/backtick values un-redacted is what keeps command-substitution smuggling (`git commit -m "$(rm -rf /)"`) caught. Backtick command-substitution itself remains the separately-tracked, uncaught pre-existing gap (bd-bdb-backtick-bypass).

cat > /workspace/review.md <<'EOF'
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378 — `--arg label` binds the jq variable `$label`, and `label` is a jq keyword: jq 1.6 (the stock jq on Debian 12 / Ubuntu 22.04 and the version installed here) rejects the program ("unexpected label, expecting IDENT"), so `cmd_derive` aborts on the first sprint row. Every `derive` caller breaks on such hosts (`write`, `mark`, the /loa Run line, /run-resume); 15 of the 17 RCD cases fail for this reason. Rename the variable (e.g. `$lbl`).
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:226 — the emptiness guard `jq -e 'type == "object"' <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'` (same pattern on line 223 for `$vj`) assumes jq exits non-zero on empty input; jq 1.6 exits 0, so a feedback file without a LOA-VERDICT trailer (the documented legacy fallback) leaves `pj` empty, `--argjson p ''` fails and `fb_parse` prints nothing. `record-round` then dies with exit 2 instead of hashing the findings section (RCR-7 fails) and `derive` breaks on any sprint with legacy feedback. Test `[[ -n "$pj" ]]` before the jq check.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:154 — `atomic_update` seeds a missing file with `{}`, which is an object, so `merge_breaker` (line 295, `if type == "object" then . else skeleton`) never takes the skeleton branch on `derive --write`. A breaker file created by derive therefore has no `threshold`, `limit` or `timeout.started` (verified by running the JQ_DEFS on `{}`), while the `--json` report, built from `null`, shows the full skeleton. The timeout trigger can then never fire for that run and `record-round` prints `cycle N/null`. Seed `null`, or test `.triggers` as `cmd_record_round` does on line 496.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:732 — the comment states that turning `destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier` off "only tightens". Replaying the corpus with `run-corpus.sh --knob-off` shows the opposite: D122, D123, D127, D131, D136 and D141 (a `.sh` target, a shebang body, a nested heredoc, `\rm`, a variable command word, a control character) exit 0 under the knob-off scrub and are blocked only by the classifier. The rollback key loosens the fence; the claim must go or the knob-off path must keep those checks.
head/.loa.config.yaml.example:1243 — same false "turning it off only tightens" claim in the operator-facing comment for the rollback key; an operator rolling back under that assurance re-opens the six corpus cases above.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/heredoc-classifier.sh:6 — the new library has no caller: `guard-yield.sh` is not part of this change and nothing else sources the file, yet the header says guard-yield's likely-false-positive heuristic calls it (and line 14 describes its fallback). Either wire `guard-yield.sh` to `heredoc_nonexec` as described or drop the file and the claim; shipping an unreferenced library with an untrue header misleads the next reader.
head/tests/unit/guard-yield.bats:34 — the fixture row's comment says the heredoc is classified "via lib/heredoc-classifier.sh", but `guard-yield.sh` is unchanged and still judges by `<<` presence, so the test asserts nothing about the classifier; the comment documents behaviour that does not exist.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:97 — when the config does not parse with `yq -o=json` (malformed YAML, or a non-mikefarah yq, which the decisions-surface hook and implement-gate still cater for), `cfg` is replaced by `{}` and resolution continues: every profile key then resolves to the profile default and the explicit keys are never consulted, inverting the documented "explicit key wins" precedence (e.g. an explicit `guardrails.input.enabled: false` becomes `true` under `full`). Treat an unparseable config as unresolved and fall back to `_loa_pl_live`/the caller's fallback instead.
head/.claude/scripts/test-lint-invariants.sh:257 — the good-fixture assertion is weakened from "exit 0" to "exit 0 or 1" (also line 320) without stating which WARN the fixture now produces or why it is expected; the new `check_optional_constraint_tables` emits only PASS or ERROR, so nothing in this change explains the loosening, and it hides WARN regressions in the self-test that the new LI-9 case relies on. Fix the fixture or assert the specific WARN.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED
EOF

content.text:
Review written to `/workspace/review.md`. Verdict: **CHANGES_REQUIRED**.

**What I did.** I read the full diff and the rewritten files, copied `pr/head` to a scratch directory, syntax-checked every script, and ran the suites that work on the touched set: the new implement-gate matrix (11/11 pass), the karpathy per-task suite (10/11, the one failure is a snapshot artifact: the frozen copy drops executable bits), the profile-lib suite (14/14 of the runnable cases), the fence corpus with the classifier on (all 89 benign and 142 dangerous rows correct), and the run-checkpoint suites, which exposed the main defects.

**Findings that block merge:**
- `run-checkpoint.sh` binds a jq variable named `$label`. `label` is a jq keyword, and jq 1.6 (the installed version, and the stock jq on Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04) refuses the program. `derive` aborts on every sprint row, which also breaks `write`, `mark`, the `/loa` Run line and `/run-resume`. 15 of 17 derive cases fail on this.
- The no-trailer fallback in `fb_parse` guards against empty input with `jq -e`, which exits 0 on empty input under jq 1.6. A legacy feedback file then produces `--argjson p ''`, `record-round` exits 2, and `derive` breaks on legacy sprints.
- `derive --write` seeds a missing breaker file with `{}`, so `merge_breaker` never applies the skeleton. The written breaker lacks thresholds, the cycle limit and `timeout.started`, while the report shows the full skeleton. The timeout trigger can never fire for such a run.
- The rollback knob for the heredoc classifier is documented as "only tightens" in the fence and the example config. Replaying the corpus with `--knob-off` lets six dangerous rows through that the classifier blocks.

**Lower-severity findings:** the new `heredoc-classifier.sh` library has no caller and its header claims guard-yield uses it (guard-yield is untouched); profile-lib silently drops the explicit config on a parse failure so profile defaults override explicit keys; the lint self-test was loosened from exit 0 to exit 0 or 1 without a stated cause.

**Not flagged:** the `REDACTED-TEST-SECRET` literal and missing executable bits in the bats files are artifacts of the frozen snapshot (present in base too), not defects of the change.
